items.body_text:
Despite Ukrainian strikes, Russian online marketplaces Ozon and Wildberries are still selling supplies for Russia’s military. Here’s what we found.
In early August, amid a wave of strikes on Wildberries warehouses, we looked into what goods are being ordered for the Russian army on Russian online marketplaces. It turned out that almost anything is available there, including body bags for the dead. At that time, Ukraine had not yet struck Ozon’s facilities, which fueled conspiracy theories. In the second half of August, however, Ukraine’s armed forces began hitting that company’s warehouses as well. Meduza decided to check whether the marketplaces are still selling goods that end up going to the front. Here’s what we found.
What exactly we checked
A month ago, Meduza reviewed posts in 71 Telegram channels and six VKontakte communities that raise donations for Russian soldiers. The channels’ authors often specify exactly what they’re raising money for, and sometimes post direct links to items for sale.
Those posts contained 3,709 direct links to Wildberries. Volunteers supplying the Russian army ordered both “civilian” items, such as food or clothing, and gear clearly intended for military use at the front, including body armor and drone components.
Volunteers used Ozon almost as actively: the posts contained 3,609 links and 1,025 different product listings, including similar drone components. Volodymyr Zelensky has officially cited that role in supplying drone components as the reason for the strikes on Wildberries warehouses.
Yet no targeted strikes hit Ozon facilities before August 22. By September 1, however, the strikes had become systematic.
The first target was a logistics center in Chapaevsk, in Samara region. The next day, drones hit a center in Orenburg, forcing the evacuation of more than 300 employees. On August 24, Ozon reported strikes on four more facilities: in Enem (Krasnodar Krai), Makhachkala, Adygeysk, and Nevinnomyssk (Stavropol region). Overnight on August 27, drones again struck the Orenburg facility, along with a warehouse in Ufa. Overnight on August 29, Ukrainian drones struck an Ozon logistics site in Rostov region. The following day, a strike on Belgorod damaged an Ozon sorting center and delivery hub.
After the initial strikes on the marketplace’s facilities, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry announced that now it was “Ozon’s turn,” calling the strikes themselves “long-range sanctions.” The ministry called the strikes part of a campaign against “storage centers for dual-use goods,” meant to disrupt supplies to the Russian army while also damaging the Russian economy.
What’s still for sale on Ozon: drone drop systems, exoskeletons, and body armor
After Ukraine began striking Ozon, we rechecked every link to the marketplace that had appeared in the channels and communities of pro-Russian volunteers. We found 604 of the 1,025 items still available for purchase.
Another 313 listings remain on the marketplace, though Ozon marks them as temporarily out of stock. For 29 items, delivery is unavailable to any of the 25 Russian cities we checked. Seventy-nine listings have been removed entirely.
Among the 1,000 items, we separately identified 51 whose Ozon descriptions explicitly mention military or tactical use. Of those, 29 remain for sale, 13 are out of stock, two are unavailable for delivery, and six have been removed.
Ozon still sells the Exorise “Muravei” (“Ant”) assault exoskeleton for about 54,000 rubles. Also still available is an FPV video receiver for 7,500 rubles, a device that receives a real-time video feed from a drone; through it, the operator sees the picture from the onboard camera and can fly the drone “first-person.” The seller’s listing states outright that the device is well suited for use in the “SVO.”
Also still available is a cargo drop system for drones for about 5,000 rubles (Z-volunteers have ordered it along with other drone accessories). These devices let users attach a small payload to a

items.title: Kazakhstan to introduce mandatory paid electronic entry permits for foreigners starting November 1. This will also affect Russians.
items.summary: Kazakhstan has begun phasing in paid electronic entry permits for foreigners who don’t need a visa, a requirement that will also apply to Russians. Serbia’s Foreign Ministry published details of the new entry rules.
items.body_text:
Kazakhstan to introduce mandatory paid electronic entry permits for foreigners starting November 1. This will also affect Russians.
Kazakhstan has begun phasing in paid electronic entry permits for foreigners who don’t need a visa, a requirement that will also apply to Russians. Serbia’s Foreign Ministry published details of the new entry rules.
The Electronic Travel Authorization, or ETA, will be issued through the QazETA digital platform, with applications required at least 72 hours before travel. The permit is valid for 180 calendar days and allows multiple entries during that period.
Obtaining the permit through QazETA is expected to cost 3,900 thousand tenge — about 730 rubles, or 7 euros. Applying at the border will cost twice as much, 7,800 thousand tenge, or roughly 1,460 rubles and 14 euros.
Here’s what is known about how the rollout will proceed:
- From August 25 to November 1, the system will run in test mode: foreigners will still be allowed into the country without a permit, though border guards will warn travelers that one will be required on their next entry
- Starting November 1, the permit will become mandatory for travelers arriving in Kazakhstan by plane
- Starting November 15, the requirement will extend to travelers crossing the external border of the Eurasian Economic Union by car or bus — meaning Kazakhstan’s borders with China, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan
- Starting November 30, it will extend to road crossings at the Eurasian Economic Union’s internal borders, including those with Russia and Kyrgyzstan
- Starting December 15, it will be mandatory for travelers arriving by train or sea.
Kazakhstan’s Internal Affairs Ministry disclosed plans to introduce paid electronic entry permits for citizens of visa-free countries in early August, when it published a draft of the corresponding resolution. The ministry reported that the permits would be rolled out between August and December 2026, though it did not specify the stages or the cost at the time.
Serbia and Kazakhstan maintain a visa-free arrangement, and Serbia’s Foreign Ministry did not clarify where it obtained its information about the stages of Kazakhstan’s permit rollout.
Kazakhstan, which Russians can currently enter without a visa or any permit, became a major destination for Russians fleeing the country after the start of the war and the mobilization that followed. Russians who spend more than 90 days there within a six-month period must obtain a temporary residence permit.

items.title: Latvia bans imports of books, clothing, and toys made in Russia and Belarus
items.summary: A Latvian ban on imports of a range of goods made in Russia and Belarus took effect on September 1, covering not only direct imports but also goods routed through third countries.
items.body_text:
A Latvian ban on imports of a range of goods made in Russia and Belarus took effect on September 1, covering not only direct imports but also goods routed through third countries.
The banned list includes books, newspapers, and other printed materials, along with clothing, footwear, headwear, toys, games, and sporting goods.
The Latvian news outlet Delfi reports that Latvia’s restrictions don’t extend to other European Union countries: goods made in Russia or Belarus can still enter Latvia via Lithuania, and Russian and Belarusian goods may still transit through Latvia en route to other EU states.
The Saeima, Latvia’s parliament, passed the underlying amendments in late July.
Latvian officials have said the ban is meant to protect the country’s security interests, limit Russia and Belarus’s ability to profit from exports, and curb the flow of Russian propaganda materials into Latvia.

items.title: SC quashes FIRs against NEET protesters, but with a caveat for 'hardened criminals'
items.body_text:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday invoked its special powers and quashed all FIRs registered against student protesters in different parts of the country during the NEET paper leak protests.The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said the order had been passed in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and shall not be treated as a precedent.The apex court said it was invoking its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution considering the future of the students who bona fide participated in the protests.The court, however, allowed Delhi Police to pursue the FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present at the Jantar Mantar protests, citing their serious criminal antecedents.This comes a day after the Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIRs registered against student protesters over alleged violence during protests against the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, also informed the apex court that the Centre remained committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to CJP leaders during their meeting with the government.
Under the first assurance, the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25. The second was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."The Centre is committed to honouring the assurance given to CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after the NEET exam cancellation; however, three months are needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told the Supreme Court."As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Following the apex court hearing, Cockroach Janata Party called off its September 5 protest against the Centre for failing to honour the promises made to persuade the group to withdraw the agitation."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the Government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.
How CJP reacted
After the hearing, Das said welcomed SC's order but also questioned why were these 'hardend criminals' allowed to roam freely in the society in the first place."Regarding the Delhi Policeâs apprehension, based on facial recognition technology, that around 2,800 alleged hardened criminals were present at the protest site, we argued during negotiations with the government that if these 2,800 hardened criminals were indeed present, the first question was why they were roaming freely in society in the first place," Das said while talking to reporters.
"Secondly, if they committed any heinous crimes, such as rape, murder, or other grave offences, at the protest site, then they should be prosecuted, investigated, and imprisoned," he added.During a hearing on August 18 on petitions related to the student protests, Supreme Court had indicated that it was inclined to quash the FIRs by exercising its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution.The indication came after the court was informed of legal complications in withdrawing the FIRs. Once registered, the cases can be closed only through a closure report, which the concerned Magistrate has the discretion to reject.Earlier, Supreme Court had also constituted a committee to examine allegations of excessive use of force by security personnel against students during the July 20 march over the NEET paper leak.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a

NEW DELHI: Centre on Tuesday tightened the stock limit for sugar dealers, reducing it from 4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals from September 15 to November 30, as it sought to curb hoarding and contain rising retail prices.The food ministry said the existing 4,000-quintal limit would continue in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas âconsidering the specific market requirements of the regionâ.The move is aimed at ensuring adequate availability of sugar in the domestic market and preventing hoarding and speculative trading, the ministry said.Under the revised rules, dealers cannot hold sugar stocks for more than 30 days from the date of receipt. They will also not be allowed to hold more than 2,000 quintals at any time at any location across the country.The ministry said the 4,000-quintal limit would remain in place in Kolkata because the region sources sugar mainly from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplies it to eastern and northeastern states.The decision comes as sugar prices remain elevated. The pace attack is bolstered by the return of Jasprit Bumrah, alongside Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana. Notable batsmen include Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan, although some players still await fitness clearance prior to the series start.

NEW DELHI: India have announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, with Jasprit Bumrah returning to the side while Hardik Pandya misses out after suffering a fresh setback in his comeback bid.Shreyas Iyer will continue to lead the side, with Tilak Varma as his deputy. Young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who was part of the squad for the Zimbabwe series, has also retained his place.Bumrah returns to the T20I squad after missing the recent series against Ireland and England as well as the Zimbabwe tour. Sanju Samson, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana are the other players returning after missing the Zimbabwe series.As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, Pandya's comeback plans had suffered a fresh roadblock after a late leg niggle forced him to pause bowling at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. He had been progressing well in his recovery but the setback put his availability for the Afghanistan series in doubt.Pandya has not played competitive cricket since turning out for Mumbai Indians in the IPL on May 24, while his last appearance for India came in the T20 World Cup final on March 8.

items.title: Iran would 'immediately' reciprocate if U.S. returns to June deal: President Pezeshkian
items.summary: His remarks came as the Strait of Hormuz remained a key point of contention between Iran and the United States, which resumed exchanging fire on August 31 after more than a month of relative calm
items.body_text:
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) that Tehran would "immediately" reciprocate if the United States returned to a June deal aimed at ending their war.
"I state explicitly that if the United States returns to its commitments under the aforementioned memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately take reciprocal action," Mr. Pezeshkian said at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Kyrgyzstan, according to the website of the Iranian presidency.
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was aimed at ending months of hostilities between Tehran and Washington, which began in late February with the U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran that killed former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The deal later collapsed, with both sides accusing each other of violating its terms.
"The repeated violation by the United States of its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding showed that... the absence of effective enforcement guarantees and a return to a policy of pressure and threats could derail the path of diplomacy," said Mr. Pezeshkian in a later speech at the Summit.
"Iran has continued to regard diplomacy and negotiations as the primary path to resolving disputes. But diplomacy without good faith, without respect for commitments and without refraining from the use of force cannot create lasting peace," he added.
His remarks came as the Strait of Hormuz remained a key point of contention between Iran and the United States, which resumed exchanging fire on Monday (August 31, 2026) after more than a month of relative calm.
Tehran has maintained its closure of the strategic waterway, while insisting it would only open it if Washington meets its demands of lifting its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removing oil sanctions and unfreezing Iranian assets abroad under the deal.
On Monday (August 29, 2026), Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said "the United States must return to its commitments and to what their president signed" under the deal. "In that case, everything can be put back on the right track."
Published - September 01, 2026 04:40 pm IST

Flash floods, triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal on August 26. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

items.title: Nepal must make climate justice top national priority, says Environment Minister
items.summary: Nepal’s Forestry and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary said the country must assert its rights and claims on climate justice at international forums
items.body_text:
Nepal’s Forestry and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary has called for climate change and environmental issues to be made a top national priority, local media reported on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).
Follow the updates of the Nepal flash floods on September 1, 2026.
Her comments came days after devastating flash floods killed around 1,000 people in Nepal and left nearly 4,000 missing. The floods, triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.
She also said the country must assert its rights and claims on climate justice at international forums.
Speaking at a consultation with experts at the ministry before leaving to attend a ministerial conference of the least developed countries, Ms. Chaudhary said that Nepal must work to establish mountain issues on the global agenda.
The discussions also covered domestic and international initiatives to seek compensation for the severe damage caused by the recent floods, according to Nepal News.
“Unless we can present this agenda as our right and our claim, we cannot give it the priority it deserves,” she was quoted as saying by the Onlinekhabar news portal.
Nepal is a mountainous country and home to Mount Everest, the world’s highest peak, she noted, stressing the need for the country to lead the mountain agenda and establish it globally.
Ms. Chaudhary said it would be difficult to give priority at the national level to the damage and problems caused by the climate crisis unless climate justice was established as a right before the international community.
She said climate change should not be confined to one or two government programmes or international conferences.
Ms. Chaudhary also called for cooperation among civil society, experts, the media and other stakeholders, saying government efforts alone would not be sufficient to address climate and environmental challenges.

items.title: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने जंतर-मंतर प्रोटेस्ट की सभी FIR रद्द कीं:नई FIR भी दर्ज नहीं होंगी; कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने 5 सितंबर का मार्च वापस लिया
items.summary: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंगलवार को 20 से 25 जुलाई के बीच कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रदर्शनकारियों के खिलाफ दर्ज सभी FIR रद्द करने का आदेश दिया। कोर्ट ने साफ किया कि जिन प्रदर्शनकारियों का आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड है, उन्हें इस राहत का फायदा नहीं मिलेगा। यह आदेश देश के सभी राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में दर्ज मामलों पर लागू होगा। सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसले के बाद CJP ने 5 सितंबर को दिल्ली में प्रस्तावित विरोध मार्च वापस ले लिया। संगठन ने कहा कि केंद्र सरकार के आश्वासन और कोर्ट के फैसले के बाद यह फैसला लिया गया है।
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- CJP Jantar Mantar Protest FIR Case; Supreme Court Vs Delhi Police | NEET Paper Leak Row
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने जंतर-मंतर प्रोटेस्ट की सभी FIR रद्द कीं:नई FIR भी दर्ज नहीं होंगी; कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने 5 सितंबर का मार्च वापस लिया
- कॉपी लिंक
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंगलवार को 20 से 25 जुलाई के बीच कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रदर्शनकारियों के खिलाफ दर्ज सभी FIR रद्द करने का आदेश दिया।
कोर्ट ने साफ किया कि जिन प्रदर्शनकारियों का आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड है, उन्हें इस राहत का फायदा नहीं मिलेगा। यह आदेश देश के सभी राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में दर्ज मामलों पर लागू होगा।
सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसले के बाद CJP ने 5 सितंबर को दिल्ली में प्रस्तावित विरोध मार्च वापस ले लिया। संगठन ने कहा कि केंद्र सरकार के आश्वासन और कोर्ट के फैसले के बाद यह फैसला लिया गया है।
सरकार ने सोमवार को दाखिल किया था अंतरिम आवेदन
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने यह फैसला दिल्ली पुलिस के अंतरिम आवेदन पर सुनाया। अंतरिम आवेदन का मतलब है कि किसी मामले की सुनवाई चल रही हो और उसके दौरान किसी खास मुद्दे पर तुरंत राहत या आदेश की मांग के लिए कोर्ट में अलग से अर्जी दी जाए।
इस आवेदन में सरकार ने कहा था कि 25 जुलाई के सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश के बाद दिल्ली पुलिस CJP के प्रदर्शन से जुड़ी 13 FIR को आगे नहीं बढ़ाना चाहती। यानी इन मामलों में पुलिस अब कार्रवाई जारी रखने के बजाय उन्हें खत्म करना चाहती है।
कोर्ट बोला- यह फैसला संविधान के अनुच्छेद 142 के तहत लिया
सुनवाई के दौरान कोर्ट ने कहा कि FIR रद्द करने का फैसला सिर्फ इसी मामले के खास तथ्यों और हालात को देखकर लिया गया है, इसलिए इसे दूसरे मामलों के लिए उदाहरण और बाध्यकारी फैसला नहीं माना जाएगा।
कोर्ट ने यह भी कहा कि संविधान के अनुच्छेद 142 के तहत मिली अपनी विशेष शक्ति का इस्तेमाल इस शर्त पर किया जा रहा है कि दोनों पक्ष कोर्ट के सामने हुए समझौते का पूरी तरह पालन करेंगे।
अभिजीत दीपके ने कहा- यह फैसला छात्रों की जीत
- कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रवक्ता सौरव दास ने कहा, ‘अगस्त के शुरूआत में सरकार के डेलिगेशन ने हमसे बात करना बंद कर दिया था, फिर हमें लगा कि ये विश्वासघात करना चाहते हैं, इसलिए हमनें 5 सितंबर को मार्च निकालेंगे का फैसला किया। आज कोर्ट में सुनवाई हुई। पूरे देश में सारे FIR को रद्दकर दिया है। यह ऐतिहासिक पल है।’
- अभिजीत दीपके ने कहा, 'सुप्रीम कोर्ट का फैसला छात्रों की जीत है।
- कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने कहा, ‘सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने छात्रों के खिलाफ चल रहे सभी अन्यायपूर्ण मुकदमों को खारिज कर दिया है। हमारी मांगें सुनी गई हैं और अब किसी भी छात्र को आगे ऐसी कार्रवाई का सामना नहीं करना पड़ेगा। इंकलाब जिंदाबाद।’
20 जुलाई को प्रदर्शनकारियों-सुरक्षाकर्मियों में झड़प हुई थी
20 जुलाई को CJP के नेतृत्व में दिल्ली में हुए मार्च के दौरान प्रदर्शनकारियों और सुरक्षाकर्मियों के बीच झड़प हुई थी। संसद की ओर बढ़ रही भीड़ को रोकने के लिए सुरक्षाकर्मियों ने लाठीचार्ज और आंसू गैस का इस्तेमाल किया था।
इसके बाद छात्रों का आंदोलन कई शहरों तक फैल गया। उनकी मुख्य मांग तत्कालीन केंद्रीय शिक्षा मंत्री धर्मेंद्र प्रधान का इस्तीफा था।
आंदोलन 20 जून को जंतर-मंतर से शुरू हुआ था। प्रधान के इस्तीफे और सरकार की ओर से CJP की दूसरी मांगें मानने के बाद 25 जुलाई को आंदोलन खत्म कर दिया गया था।

- Hindi News
- National
- Goa Delhi Indigo Flight Emergency Landing | Mopa Airport Engine Failure
गोवा-दिल्ली फ्लाइट के इंजन में खराबी:उड़ान भरने के कुछ देर बाद 14 हजार फीट पर पता चला, गोवा एयरपोर्ट पर इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग
- कॉपी लिंक
गोवा से दिल्ली जा रही इंडिगो की फ्लाइट 6E 2102 को उड़ान भरने के कुछ मिनट बाद एक इंजन में तकनीकी खराबी की सूचना मिली। इसके बाद विमान को वापस मनोहर इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट लाया गया।
फ्लाइट ने सुबह 9:16 बजे उड़ान भरी थी और 9:30 बजे सुरक्षित लैंडिंग की। Flightradar24 के डेटा के मुताबिक वापस मुड़ते समय विमान करीब 14 हजार फीट की ऊंचाई पर था। विमान में 229 यात्री सवार थे।
इंजन में खराबी के कारणों की जांच शुरू
इंडिगो ने बताया कि विमान की फिलहाल मेंटेनेंस जांच की जा रही है। सभी जरूरी मंजूरियां मिलने के बाद ही विमान दोबारा उड़ान भरेगा।
कंपनी ने कहा कि असुविधा को कम करने के लिए यात्रियों को खाने-पीने की चीजें उपलब्ध कराई गईं और उन्हें समय-समय पर जानकारी दी गई। यात्रियों के लिए वैकल्पिक व्यवस्था भी की गई है।
12 अगस्त: इंडिगो फ्लाइट की चेन्नई में इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग
चेन्नई एयरपोर्ट पर 12 अगस्त की देर रात एक इंडिगो फ्लाइट की इमरजेंसी लैंडिग कराई गई थी। फ्लाइट कोलकाता से चेन्नई जा रही थी। फ्लाइट चेन्नई में लैंड करने वाली थी, तभी पायलट ने महसूस किया कि बायां इंजन फेल हो गया है।
उसने तुरंत एयर ट्रैफिक कंट्रोल (ATC) को इसकी जानकारी दी, जिसके बाद चेन्नई एयरपोर्ट पर रात 11:29 बजे फुल इमरजेंसी घोषित की गई। इसके बाद फ्लाइट की सुरक्षित लैंडिंग हुई। विमान में 224 लोग सवार थे। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
4 अगस्त: एअर इंडिया फ्लाइट अचानक 300 फीट नीचे आई, 17 घायल
थाइलैंड के फुकेट से दिल्ली आ रही एअर इंडिया की फ्लाइट 4 अगस्त को अचानक करीब 300 फीट नीचे आ गई थी। घटना ओडिशा के झारसुगुड़ा के पास हुई, जब एयरबस A320 करीब 36,220 फीट की ऊंचाई पर उड़ रहा था। हालांकि, बाद में फ्लाइट की दिल्ली में सुरक्षित लैंडिंग हुई। घटना में 17 यात्री घायल हुए थे।
शुरुआत में एअर इंडिया ने घटना को टर्बुलेंस बताया था। बाद में एयरलाइन ने अपने बयान से ‘टर्बुलेंस’ शब्द हटा दिया और इसे सिर्फ ‘क्रूज के दौरान अचानक ऊंचाई कम होना’ बताया। DGCA मामले की जांच कर रहा है। हालांकि, अभी यह साफ नहीं है कि घटना की असली वजह क्या थी। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
27 जुलाई: दुबई-मुंबई इंडिगो फ्लाइट की राजकोट में इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग
दुबई से मुंबई आ रही इंडिगो की इंटरनेशनल फ्लाइट को पिछले महीने 27 जुलाई को गुजरात के राजकोट एयरपोर्ट पर इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग करनी पड़ी थी।
उड़ान के दौरान पायलटों को विमान के निचले कार्गो होल्ड में धुआं होने का अलर्ट मिला। इसके बाद क्रू ने तुरंत इमरजेंसी घोषित की।
पायलटों ने राजकोट ATC से प्राथमिकता के आधार पर लैंडिंग की अनुमति मांगी। ATC ने विमान को सुरक्षित उतारने के लिए जरूरी व्यवस्था की।
एहतियात के तौर पर रनवे के पास फायर टेंडर और मेडिकल टीमों को तैनात किया गया था। इमरजेंसी रिस्पॉन्स टीमों को अलर्ट रखने के बाद विमान की सुरक्षित लैंडिंग कराई गई।
-------------
ये खबर भी पढ़ें…
एअर इंडिया की सऊदी अरब-दिल्ली फ्लाइट में बम की धमकी:क्रू को टॉयलेट में धमकी लिखा टिश्यू पेपर मिला; अहमदाबाद में इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग
सऊदी अरब के दम्माम से दिल्ली आ रही एअर इंडिया की फ्लाइट में सोमवार को बम की धमकी मिलने के बाद अहमदाबाद एयरपोर्ट पर इमरजेंसी लैंडिंग कराई गई। उड़ान के दौरान क्रू मेंबर को विमान के टॉयलेट में एक टिश्यू पेपर मिला, जिस पर अंग्रेजी में ‘बम’ लिखा था। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…

भास्कर अपडेट्स:केंद्रीय मंत्री चिराग पासवान को जान से मारने की धमकी मिली, गृह सचिव को दी जानकारी
- कॉपी लिंक
केंद्रीय मंत्री और LJP(R) के अध्यक्ष चिराग पासवान को मंगलवार को जान से मारने की धमकी मिली। डाक से मिले लेटर में लिखा है- कट्टर आतंकवादी जल्द ही आपकी हत्या कर देंगे। मंत्री के कार्यालय ने उन्हें मिली धमकी के बारे में केंद्रीय गृह सचिव को पत्र लिखा है।
आज की अन्य बड़ी खबरें…
PM मोदी शिक्षक दिवस पर Gen-Z के साथ सीधे बात करेंगे, दिल्ली के श्रीराम कॉलेज ऑफ कॉमर्स में होगा प्रोग्राम
PM नरेंद्र मोदी शिक्षक दिवस पर 5 सितंबर को दिल्ली यूनिवर्सिटी के श्रीराम कॉलेज ऑफ कॉमर्स में युवाओं और Gen-Z के साथ सीधे बातचीत करेंगे।
सरकार के आश्वासन के बाद CJP ने 5 सितंबर को होने वाला मार्च रद्द किया
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) के सौरव दास सुप्रीम कोर्ट के सामने पेश हुए और कहा कि प्रदर्शनकारियों के खिलाफ दर्ज मामलों को वापस लेने के लिए केंद्र द्वारा उठाए गए कदमों को देखते हुए CJP ने 5 सितंबर को प्रस्तावित मार्च का आह्वान वापस ले लिया है।
वहीं, सरकार की ओर से कोर्ट में पेश हुए सॉलिसिटर जनरल तुषार मेहता ने कहा कि छात्रों के विरोध प्रदर्शन के बाद CJP नेताओं को दी गई तीनों आश्वासनों को पूरा करने के लिए केंद्र सरकार पूरी तरह प्रतिबद्ध है।
महाराष्ट्र के नांदेड में जीप पेड़ से टकराई, 3 की मौत, 7 घायल
महाराष्ट्र के नांदेड में तेज रफ्तार जीप सड़क किनारे पेड़ से टकरा गई। हादसे में तीन लोगों की मौत हो गई, जबकि सात लोग गंभीर रूप से घायल हुए हैं। पुलिस ने मंगलवार को यह जानकारी दी।
हादसा सोमवार शाम करीब 6 बजे तोटांबा फॉरेस्ट घाट में हुआ। पुलिस के मुताबिक, हादसे में जान गंवाने वाले और घायल सभी लोग तेलंगाना के निर्मल जिले के रहने वाले थे।
सभी लोग नांदेड में झरना देखने और मंदिर में दर्शन करने आए थे। वापस घर लौटते समय ड्राइवर ने जीप से नियंत्रण खो दिया। इसके बाद जीप सड़क से उतरकर किनारे लगे एक बड़े पेड़ से जा टकराई। टक्कर इतनी जोरदार थी कि जीप बुरी तरह क्षतिग्रस्त हो गई।
तेलंगाना में BJP-कांग्रेस कार्यकर्ताओं में झड़प, एक-दूसरे के दफ्तर और घर पर हमले
तेलंगाना के नलगोंडा में BJP और कांग्रेस कार्यकर्ताओं के बीच सोमवार रात झड़प हो गई। आरोप है कि कांग्रेस कार्यकर्ताओं ने BJP जिलाध्यक्ष नागम वार्षित रेड्डी के घर में तोड़फोड़ की। पुलिस ने स्थिति संभालने के लिए मंत्री कोमाटिरेड्डी वेंकट रेड्डी के कैंप ऑफिस और BJP जिला कार्यालय पर सुरक्षा बढ़ा दी।
यह विवाद सोमवार को BJP कार्यकर्ताओं द्वारा मंत्री के कैंप ऑफिस में कथित तोड़फोड़ के बाद शुरू हुआ। इससे पहले यूथ कांग्रेस के प्रदर्शन के दौरान BJP कार्यालय के गेट पर काला रंग फेंका गया था। पुलिस के मुताबिक, अभी दोनों पक्षों की ओर से कोई औपचारिक शिकायत नहीं मिली है और मामले की जांच जारी है।
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने महुआ मोइत्रा के कैश-फॉर-क्वेरी मामले में सुनवाई टाली, केंद्र की ओर से कोई पेश नहीं हुआ
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मंगलवार को TMC सांसद महुआ मोइत्रा से जुड़े कैश-फॉर-क्वेरी मामले में लोकपाल की ओर से दायर दो याचिकाओं पर सुनवाई टाल दी। CJI सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्या बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की बेंच ने मामले की सुनवाई की। बेंच ने कहा कि 24 जुलाई को केंद्र सरकार को मामले में पक्षकार बनाया गया था, लेकिन मंगलवार की सुनवाई में उसकी ओर से कोई प्रतिनिधि मौजूद नहीं था। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 24 जुलाई को इन याचिकाओं में केंद्रीय गृह मंत्रालय को पक्षकार बनाया था। लोकपाल ने दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट के उस फैसले को चुनौती दी है, जिसमें CBI को महुआ मोइत्रा के खिलाफ चार्जशीट दाखिल करने की मंजूरी देने से जुड़े लोकपाल के आदेश को रद्द कर दिया गया था।
विनेश फोगाट की याचिका पर दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट ने भारतीय कुश्ती महासंघ से जवाब मांगा, अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई का मामला

items.summary: SC uses special powers to cancel FIRs against protesters CJP praises historic move
items.body_text:
SC uses special powers to cancel FIRs against protesters, CJP praises historic move
The Supreme Court invoked Article 142 to cancel FIRs against paper leak protesters over incidents between July 20 and 25, barring states and UTs from registering fresh cases. It allowed the Centre and Delhi Police to proceed against 2,873 persons. The court also ordered a compensation framework, while CJP praised the move as "historic."
The Supreme Court on Tuesday invoked its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to cancel all FIRs listed before it against youth protesters over incidents between July 20 and 25 during the Cockroach Janta Party-led paper leak protests across the country, which demanded then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. The court said any other FIRs related to the same incidents in any state or Union Territory should not be pursued or investigated and would be treated as closed for all purposes.
Allowing applications filed by five states seeking the cancelling of the FIRs, the Supreme Court said no state or Union Territory should register any fresh FIR for incidents between July 20 and 26.
THE ONLY EXCEPTION
The court, however, said the Centre and Delhi Police would remain at liberty to register fresh FIRs against 2,873 persons, as described in their application, without prejudice to the affected parties' right to seek legal remedy.
The government, earlier, placed before the court a specific application by the Delhi Police seeking permission to register a fresh FIR against 2,873 people who were alleged to have serious criminal records, but only if an investigation established their involvement in offences involving bodily harm or destruction of property during the protests.
Mehta said the request was peculiar to Delhi and sought leave to file a fresh FIR only against those 2,873 individuals if their involvement in such offences was established. He added that the proposed action would not be a blanket exception covering all protesters.
Talking about the only rider in the Supreme Court's order, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said that if the 2,800 alleged hardened criminals were indeed present at the protest site and had committed serious crimes such as rape, murder or other heinous acts, they should be prosecuted, investigated and imprisoned.
"Regarding the Delhi Police’s apprehension, based on facial recognition technology, that around 2,800 alleged hardened criminals were present at the protest site, we argued during negotiations with the government that if these 2,800 hardened criminals were indeed present, the first question was why they were roaming freely in society in the first place," Das told media personnel, reported news agency ANI.
The Supreme Court said its decision to invoke Article 142 was based on commitments made before it by the central government and some states, along with a statement read by the CJP co-convenor.
It also took into account the future prospects of young protesters who had "bona fide" come to participate in peaceful protests.
On compensation, the court directed that modalities for a pan-India mechanism be worked out in consultation with states and Union Territories, with the framework adopted as a regular mechanism for compensatory measures.
The central government was also directed to provide compensation within three months in cases of suicides due to NEET 2026. Reacting to the order, a CJP spokesperson thanked the Supreme Court and described the decision as "historic."
CJP WITHDRAWS SEPTEMBER 5 PROTEST CALL
The Cockroach Janta Party told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that it was withdrawing its call for a fresh protest march in Delhi on September 5 after the government assured the court that it would honour its commitments to protesters, including the withdrawal of FIRs linked to the July 20 Jantar Mantar agitation.

items.title: 1,003 bodies recovered in Nepal floods; 4,000 still missing as rescue ops continue
items.summary: bodies recovered in Nepal floods still missing as rescue ops continue
items.body_text:
1,003 bodies recovered in Nepal floods; 4,000 still missing as rescue ops continue
As rescue teams battle rain and fresh alerts, Kathmandu is linking the disaster to climate change and seeking compensation from major emitters.
Nepal is battling the aftermath of catastrophic flash floods that have killed more than 1,000 people, left thousands missing and caused widespread destruction across the country.
The disaster was triggered after a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border sent a massive surge of water down the Bhotekoshi River, sweeping through settlements and damaging roads, bridges and hydropower projects.
Rescue operations are continuing on a massive scale, but intermittent rainfall and warnings of fresh floods have complicated efforts to reach affected areas.
DEATH TOLL CROSSES 1,000, THOUSANDS MISSING
The death toll has risen to 1,003 as security forces recover more bodies across eight affected districts.
Chitwan has reported the highest toll at 321, followed by Nawalparasi East with 216 deaths.
Around 4,000 people, including 583 foreign nationals, remain missing, raising fears that the toll could climb further. Nearly 12,000 people have been rescued so far.
The Nepalese government has deployed more than 21,300 security personnel for search, rescue and relief operations.
Helicopters are making repeated sorties to evacuate people stranded in inaccessible areas and deliver food and other essential supplies to communities cut off by the floods.
FRESH FLOOD THREAT KEEPS NEPAL ON ALERT
Even as rescue teams search for survivors, Nepal faces the threat of further flooding.
Authorities have issued fresh warnings across parts of eastern, central and western Nepal amid intermittent rainfall and rising river levels.
Rasuwa and Nuwakot are among the areas facing heightened risks, while alerts have been issued for several other districts.
Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha on Tuesday held discussions with officials from the energy and meteorology departments and other experts to assess weather conditions and possible flood risks in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and other affected areas.
The government is now focusing on continuous river monitoring, improving early warning systems and speeding up measures to reduce the risk of another disaster.
Authorities are also working to install monitoring cameras and satellite-based communication systems in vulnerable areas.
The system will transmit information from remote locations to forecasting centres and feed it into Nepal's 24-hour flood warning service, allowing authorities to track river conditions and detect signs of flooding earlier.
FLOODS WASH AWAY BRIDGES, DISRUPT KEY HIGHWAYS
The floods have caused extensive damage to Nepal's transport network, cutting off communities and disrupting movement between Kathmandu and other parts of the country.
At least 19 motorable bridges have been washed away, while highways and arterial roads have been damaged or blocked.
Sections of the highway at Krishnabhir in Dhading district were washed away, forcing authorities to introduce one-way traffic arrangements on the Prithvi and Tribhuvan highways.
Traffic between Kathmandu and Hetauda has been diverted through different routes depending on the direction of travel and the size of vehicles.
Smaller passenger vehicles travelling from Kathmandu to Hetauda have been directed through the Farping-Fakhel-Kulekhani-Bhimfedi route, while those travelling towards Kathmandu have been asked to take the Bhimfedi-Kulekhani-Sisneri-Dakshinkali route.
Separate routes have been designated for larger passenger and cargo vehicles to ease congestion on the damaged road network.
NEPAL-CHINA TRADE LINK TAKES A HIT
The destruction has also affected Nepal's key overland trade connection with China through the Rasuwagadhi border crossing.
Damage to roads and bridges in the northern districts has disrupted movement along the route, which is an important gateway for trade between the two countries.

items.body_text:
Pakistan PMO crops PM Modi out of SCO group photo, India shares full pic
The photograph was taken during the SCO summit in Bishkek on Tuesday, featuring leaders of the 10 member countries posing together.
Pakistan, being Pakistan, resorted to petty social media antics during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi was cropped out of the SCO leaders' group photograph shared by the Pakistan PMO. The cropped photo tactfully placed Shehbaz Sharif in the middle. However, the family photograph posted by PM Modi showed the full group, including Sharif.
The photograph was taken during the SCO summit in Bishkek on Tuesday, featuring leaders of the 10 member countries posing together. However, in the image posted by the Pakistan PMO, PM Modi, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and a few other leaders have been cropped out.
Moments later, amid a backlash, Sharif posted the full group photo from his personal X account.
PAKISTAN CROPS OUT MODI FROM SCO PIC
The cropped version of the photograph appeared carefully framed to place Shehbaz Sharif at the centre of the group. It sought to give the impression of Sharif occupying a more prominent position.
However, the original picture, tweeted by PM Modi, showed that it was far from reality. Sharif was, in fact, standing fourth from the right, as you can see in the above image.
It did not end there. Sharif's official account on Facebook also cropped PM Modi out of a video showing the SCO leaders' roundtable in Bishkek. Check the screenshot below.
Social media users, however, saw through Pakistan's immature social media theatrics. Several also posted the full family photograph to counter Pakistan's propaganda.
Some even edited the photo to place a "begging bowl" in Sharif's hands - a hark back to the Pakistan PM's earlier remark that he had to go around the world seeking financial help.
"Pakistan PM cropped the image to not show PM Modi. Meanwhile, Modi shared the full pic. Typical Pakistani mindset," one user posted on X.
Another user, a journalist, called it a "terrible crop job". "Imagine taking the SCO presidency and your very first foreign policy move is a terrible crop job. The Pakistan PMO digital team was so desperate to put Shehbaz Sharif in the centre that they edited out 5 world leaders," he posted.
In contrast, PM Modi's social media post featured the full SCO group photo, including Shehbaz Sharif.
BIG MOMENTS FROM SCO SUMMIT
Meanwhile, Sharif's antics at the summit drew considerable attention. The Pakistani PM was seen rushing to Russian President Vladimir Putin immediately after the family photograph.
As Putin walked away from the podium, Sharif was seen stopping him by grabbing his hand and then engaging him in a conversation.
In contrast, PM Modi was seen warmly engaging with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Putin during the SCO Summit. The trio were seen shaking hands and having a brief chat - reminiscent of the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, where the three leaders were seen chatting and sharing a laugh.
That photograph in 2025 broke the internet and quickly became one of the most defining images of the summit.
PM MODI TALKS TOUGH ON TERRORISM
On Tuesday, terrorism was at the heart of PM Modi's address at the SCO Summit, even though he did not explicitly name Pakistan.
The Prime Minister emphasised that there can be no "double standards" in the fight against terrorism, and called for dismantling its entire ecosystem, including financing.
"Those countries that use terrorism as an instrument of their policy, and provide support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism cannot be a strategic asset for anyone," PM Modi underlined without mincing his words.

items.title: Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana covers 12,467 Sepsis, Septic Shock Treatments worth rs 51.58 cr
items.summary: Punjab’s Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana data highlight the growing medical and financial burden of sepsis, underscoring the need for early recognition, timely treatment and financial protection.
items.body_text:
An infection that may initially appear routine can become life-threatening within hours when it progresses to sepsis and septic shock.
Punjab’s Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana (MMSY) has recorded 12,467 treatments for sepsis and septic shock, worth Rs 51.58 crore, till September 1, highlighting both the medical and financial burden of the condition.
Of these, severe sepsis accounted for 10,961 treatments worth Rs 44.33 crore, while 1,506 septic-shock treatments involved Rs 7.25 crore. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), sepsis is the body’s extreme response to an infection and can rapidly lead to tissue damage, organ failure and death. Almost any infection can trigger sepsis, with infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and gastrointestinal tract among the common sources.
Sepsis is not simply an infection. As the body’s response becomes dysregulated, organs may begin to malfunction. In severe cases, falling blood pressure and inadequate blood flow can progress to septic shock.
Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Balbir Singh stressed the importance of timely recognition. “Sepsis can become progressively more dangerous. When it leads to serious circulatory problems and inadequate blood flow to vital organs, the patient may progress to septic shock,” he said.
Patients with septic shock may require intensive care, intravenous fluids, antibiotics, medicines to support blood pressure, oxygen or mechanical ventilation and, in some cases, support for failing organs. Such treatment can quickly become expensive, making financial protection particularly important for families.
The Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana provides cashless health coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh per family annually to eligible families, helping reduce the financial barrier to critical treatment.
The scheme’s sepsis figures underline how such financial protection can matter when treatment requirements escalate rapidly.
The threat is especially acute among newborns. Dr Shashi Kant Dhir, Professor and Head, Department of Pediatrics, Guru Gobind Singh Medical College, Faridkot, said subtle changes in a newborn should not be ignored. “In newborns, even a small change in behaviour can be an important warning sign,” he said, adding that premature and low-birth-weight babies could deteriorate within hours.
Poor feeding, unusual sleepiness, feeling cold and changes in breathing can signal serious illness in a newborn and require urgent medical assessment.
Antibiotics remain essential when a bacterial infection is suspected or confirmed, but inappropriate use can fuel antimicrobial resistance. Self-medication, using leftover antibiotics or stopping treatment without medical advice can make infections harder to treat.
The CDC identifies confusion, difficulty breathing, extreme pain or discomfort, fever or unusually low temperature, clammy skin and rapid heart rate among warning signs requiring urgent attention.
Sepsis therefore demands action on two fronts: rapid medical recognition and treatment, and protection against catastrophic healthcare costs. The Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana data underline the scale of the financial burden, while the clinical message is simple: when a patient with an infection suddenly deteriorates, delay can cost both money and, more importantly, a life.

items.body_text:
18th BRICS Leaders' Summit: Those making their way through New Delhi on 1st September, 2026, would have to face numerous traffic regulations and carefully planned road closure measures from 11 AM to 3 PM in light of motorcade rehearsals before the upcoming 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. The advisory issued by Delhi Police provides commuters with an overview of controlled routes, prohibited areas, and alternate routes to avoid the impact of the rehearsal security perimeter.
It is highly advised to plan ahead and provide additional time for traveling to avoid significant delays.

Russia is stepping up its defence push towards India, with the S-500 Prometheus air defence system and the Su-57 fifth-generation fighter at the centre of its latest offer. The move comes as India faces two major challenges: strengthening its air defence network and addressing the shortage of fighter aircraft in the Indian Air Force (IAF).
The renewed Russian pitch comes amid a fresh meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on Monday, 31st August, with the two leaders also expected to meet again in New Delhi. NDTV’s Shiv Aroor contends that, for Moscow, the discussions are an opportunity to build on decades of defence cooperation, even as India increasingly looks towards other suppliers and its own defence industry.

The S-500 Prometheus is being presented by Russia as the next major step in its air and missile defence cooperation with India. Moscow’s pitch comes after the S-400 systems already inducted by India gained significant attention during Operation Sindoor last year.
India deployed its Russian-made S-400 systems against Pakistani aerial threats during the operation. An S-400 system was also reported to have brought down a Pakistani airborne early warning and control aircraft from a very long range, further strengthening the system’s reputation within the Indian military.
Russia appears keen to build on that experience. Just a day before the Modi-Putin meeting in Bishkek, Moscow reportedly submitted a proposal to supply India with five additional S-400 squadrons. If accepted, the deal could potentially double the number of squadrons already contracted.
However, the S-500 proposal is not a straightforward decision for India. New Delhi is already working on its own long-range air defence capabilities. Project Kusha is being developed as an indigenous system in the S-400 class, while India’s ballistic missile defence programme is also at an advanced stage.
This means India will have to examine whether the S-500 would fill an actual capability gap or simply overlap with systems that the country is already developing. Any purchase would also have to be considered in the context of India’s growing push for defence self-reliance.
Su-57 offer comes amid IAF fighter shortage
The second offer from Moscow is even more complicated for India. Russia’s second offer is the Su-57 Felon, its fifth-generation stealth fighter. The proposal comes at a time when the IAF is struggling with a shortage of fighter squadrons and India’s indigenous Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) is still years away from becoming operational.
Russia has indicated that technology transfer, greater localisation and even production in India could be part of a potential Su-57 arrangement. The IAF has also considered the Russian offer, with the aircraft being viewed as a possible “stopgap” until the AMCA becomes available.
That, however, highlights the difficult choice facing India. If New Delhi waits for the AMCA, the IAF could be left without an indigenous fifth-generation fighter for several years. But importing the Su-57 would bring its own financial, logistical and strategic complications.
The urgency has increased because India’s neighbours are also moving ahead with stealth aircraft. items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count

items.summary: "These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
items.body_text:
'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
- World News
- 3 min read
Ankara: Turkiye on Wednesday rejected Israel's claim that its airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur military airport were linked to a planned Turkish troop deployment, saying the allegations "lack seriousness" and seek to legitimise strikes on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In a post on X, the Turkish Presidential Communications Directorate said, “The allegations put forward by the Israeli Prime Ministry, which lack seriousness, aim to legitimize Israel's unlawful airstrikes targeting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.” It added, "The accusations raised stem from Netanyahu's intent to continue his expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of elections in Israel."
Turkiye said it supports the establishment of lasting peace in the region, adding that "the sole path to this lies in Netanyahu abandoning his aggressive and coercive policies and demonstrating respect for international law". "Turkey will steadfastly continue its cooperation with the Syrian Government on legitimate grounds to establish peace, stability, and prosperity in Syria, and will never allow Syria to be destabilized," it said.
The remarks came after Israel carried out airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Syria's eastern Idlib province. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said that Syria was allowing Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (local time), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the strikes "yet another very worrying violation" of Syria's territorial integrity and airspace.
Advertisement
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
In a statement, the ministry said Egypt "fully rejects" Israel's continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and warned that the strikes could further destabilise Syria at a critical time when the country requires support to restore stability and pursue political solutions. Cairo called on the international community to "assume its responsibilities" by putting an end to repeated Israeli violations and adopting firm measures to deter actions that could fuel a broader regional conflict.
Advertisement
Earlier on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel and Syria had agreed to maintain a security "status quo". In a post on X, Netanyahu's office said, "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," the statement said.
"Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added. Meanwhile, US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack expressed concern over the Israeli airstrikes, calling them an "unnecessary escalation". "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.
The airbase was targeted in four airstrikes, marking the first reported attack on the facility since the fall of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.

items.title: 'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days
items.summary: Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
items.body_text:
'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
- World News
- 2 min read
Ottawa: With Ottawa and Washington continually engaged in discussions over the 50 per cent tariff on a select range of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the implementation of the tariffs has been postponed until August 21.
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
"Over the last number of weeks, Canada has engaged in intensive discussions with the United States to address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families," he said.
The Canadian Prime Minister observed that while significant headway has been made, key work remains to be done. Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done. As this work is ongoing, the United States has agreed to postpone the implementation of its 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods under Section 338 of the U.S. Tariff Act of 1930 until the end of day, August 21," he said.
Advertisement
The announcement comes in the nick of time as the Trump administration's latest round of tariffs was originally scheduled to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday.
According to Canadian public broadcaster CBC, the levies would have applied to hundreds of products worth more than USD 28 billion, from plywood and cement to wine and hockey sticks.
Advertisement
His remarks come shortly after US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) announced a three-day pause on the 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian imports that were due to take effect the following morning, saying the United States and Canada had reached a deal subject to the finalisation of documents.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, “I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for a three day period, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!”
The three-day pause is expected to provide additional time for negotiations between the two countries. Talks intensified last week, with Canadian officials holding discussions with Trump's negotiating team in Washington.

items.title: Supreme Court Cancels Jantar Mantar Protest FIRs; CJP Calls It 'Historic' Win
items.summary: Supreme Court Cancels Jantar Mantar Protest FIRs; CJP Calls It 'Historic' Win
items.body_text:
The Supreme Court allowed Delhi Police to pursue FIRs against 2,873 individuals from the Jantar Mantar protests. This was due to their serious criminal antecedents, with the order passed under Article 142.
Supreme Court Cancels Jantar Mantar Protest FIRs; CJP Calls It 'Historic' Win
Supreme Court cancels all FIRs linked to Jantar Mantar protests, stops related probes in other states. CJP withdraws September 5 protest call after Centre's assurances.
- Supreme Court allowed FIRs against 2,873 Jantar Mantar protesters.
- Centre assured no new protest FIRs; states sought quashing.
- CJP withdrew protest call; court urged suicide compensation policy.
The Supreme Court has cancelled all FIRs related to the Jantar Mantar protest.
Chief Justice of India said the court was passing the order while accepting the applications under Article 142 of the Constitution.
The court also directed that if any FIRs related to the same matters have been registered in any other state, the investigation into those cases should be stopped.
Also Read: CJP Calls Off September 5 India Gate Protest After Centre’s Assurance On FIRs
After the SC decision, the CJP took the X account and called it a big victory for the Students.
"The Supreme Court has dismissed the unjust legal cases against students. Our demands have been heard, and no student will face such action anymore. Inquilab Zindabad!" the CJP posted on X.
Centre, States Asked To Frame Compensation Policy
The Supreme Court also said the Centre should consult the states and formulate a new policy on compensation for the families of students who died by suicide due to examinations.
Saurabh Das folded his hands and thanked the judges. The Chief Justice conveyed his best wishes to him.
Bihar, Assam, Bengal, Maharashtra Also File Pleas
Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta told the court that the Centre, through the Delhi Police, along with the governments of Bihar, Assam, West Bengal and Maharashtra, had filed applications seeking to quash FIRs linked to the student protests.
Mehta said the applications were filed to honour the assurance given by the Centre to leaders of the CJP on July 25.
He also assured the court that no future FIRs would be registered in connection with protest-related events between July 20 and July 25.
CJP Withdraws September 5 Protest Call
Following the Centre's assurance and the Supreme Court's decision, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das told the top court that the organisation had decided to withdraw its call for a September 5 protest.

The development comes after the Centre's positive response to the demands raised by the protesters and the court's decision on the FIRs.

The court directed that investigations into any FIRs related to the same protest matters, if registered in other states, should be stopped. This ensures a consistent approach to the cases.

The Supreme Court asked the Centre to consult states and formulate a new policy on compensation. This policy is for families of students who died by suicide due to examinations.

items.title: CJP Calls Off September 5 India Gate Protest After Centre’s Assurance On FIRs
items.summary: CJP Calls Off September 5 India Gate Protest After Centre’s Assurance On FIRs
items.body_text:
CJP Calls Off September 5 India Gate Protest After Centre’s Assurance On FIRs
The CJP has called off its September 5 protest after the Centre assured the Supreme Court it would close FIRs against NEET protesters and compensate affected families.
- Families of suicide victims to receive compensation from Centre.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Tuesday withdrew its proposed September 5 protest march in Delhi after the Centre assured the Supreme Court that it would facilitate the closure of FIRs against students involved in the NEET paper leak protests and provide compensation to families of students who died by suicide following the examination controversy. The development came during a hearing before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, where CJP co-convenor Saurav Das informed the bench of the decision.
FIRs In Focus
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta urged the Supreme Court to exercise its powers to close FIRs registered against NEET protesters across the country between July 20 and July 25.
Mehta said the Centre remained committed to assurances given to CJP leaders and would compensate families of students who died by suicide after the NEET examination was cancelled.
He sought three months to finalise the modalities for making the payments. The court was also told that steps were being considered to address cases arising from the protests, which had drawn allegations of police excesses against participating students.
Protest Called Off
The CJP had announced a protest march in Delhi for September 5, coinciding with Teachers' Day. The organisation had alleged that the Centre had failed to honour commitments made on July 25, when its leaders agreed to withdraw a 36-day agitation over alleged irregularities in examinations and the NEET paper leak.
The proposed march was expected to be led by families of students who had died by suicide after the cancellation of the NEET examination and the subsequent re-test.
Families of students who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July protests were expected to participate.
With the Centre reiterating its commitment before the Supreme Court, the CJP said it had decided to cancel the September 5 demonstration.
The controversy around the NEET examination triggered protests, with students and activists demanding accountability over alleged irregularities, action against those responsible and relief for affected candidates.

items.title: Pakistan Removes PM Modi From SCO Group Photo, Later Posts Full Picture
items.summary: Pakistan Removes PM Modi From SCO Group Photo, Later Posts Full Picture
items.body_text:
Pakistan sparked controversy by removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi from an SCO Summit 2026 group photograph. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif then shared this edited image on his X account.
Pakistan Removes PM Modi From SCO Group Photo, Later Posts Full Picture
Pakistan sparked controversy by cropping PM Modi out of its SCO Summit group photo, while Modi shared the full image showing Shehbaz Sharif. Modi had also criticised terrorism at the summit.
- Pakistan sparked controversy sharing a cropped SCO group photo.
- PM Modi was removed from Pakistan's shared image.
- Modi's account shared the original photo, including Sharif.
Pakistan has sparked controversy by removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi from an SCO Summit 2026 group photograph and sharing the edited image on social media.
Pakistan Prime Minister office shared the cropped photograph on the X account, and later Shehbaz Sharif shared the group photograph in its original form, which also included PM Modi.
 Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in a group photo with heads of States at the SCO Council of Heads of State Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan on 1 September 2026. pic.twitter.com/3lsruWHaYV
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) September 1, 2026
Pakistan PMO Shares Cropped SCO Group Photo
The Pakistan Prime Minister’s Office shared a post on X on Tuesday (September 1) featuring two photographs from the SCO Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.
In the images shared by the Pakistan PMO, PM Modi had been cropped out of the group photograph. The post was captioned: “Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in a group photo with Heads of State at the SCO Council of Heads of State Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on 1 September 2026.”
Later, Shehbaz Sharif shared the full image.
 Today, I was honoured to address the SCO Council of Heads of State Meeting in Bishkek as Pakistan assumed the SCO Chairmanship for 2027. I congratulated the Kyrgyz Republic on successfully hosting the Summit and steering the Organization with distinction.
Guided by the Shanghai… pic.twitter.com/1mvRW85klD
PM Modi Shares Full Group Photograph
In contrast, the photograph shared from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official X account showed the complete group, with Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif also visible.
 From the SCO Summit in Bishkek. pic.twitter.com/GDlPpVkSLR
— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 1, 2026
The contrasting posts drew attention to the fact that Modi appeared in the original group photograph shared by his own account, while he was removed from the version posted by the Pakistan PMO.
PM Modi Targets Terrorism At SCO Summit
The development came after PM Modi made strong remarks on terrorism during his address at the SCO Summit.
Without naming Pakistan, Modi called for an end to terrorism and urged countries to dismantle the entire ecosystem supporting terrorist activities, including financial networks.
“We must eliminate the entire ecosystem of terrorism and also stop the financial support it receives. We must say with one voice that there can be no room for double standards in dealing with terrorism,” Modi said.
Frequently Asked Questions
What controversy did Pakistan spark regarding the SCO Summit group photograph?
How did PM Modi's shared photograph differ from Pakistan's?
PM Modi's official X account shared the complete group photograph, which included Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif. Conversely, the version posted by the Pakistan PMO had PM Modi cropped out.
When and where did the SCO Summit mentioned in the article take place?
The SCO Council of Heads of State Summit took place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. It was held on September 1, 2026.

items.title: टीम इंडिया का ऐलान, संजू सैमसन की वापसी, रिंकू समेत 8 खिलाड़ी बाहर
items.summary: अफगानिस्तान के खिलाफ 13 सितंबर से शुरू होने वाली 3 मैचों की टी20 सीरीज के लिए टीम इंडिया का ऐलान हो गया है. श्रेयस अय्यर कप्तान और तिलक वर्मा उपकप्तान होंगे. संजू सैमसन की टीम में वापसी हुई है. बुमराह, हर्षित, वाशिंगटन और नीतीश का चयन फिटनेस टेस्ट पास करने की शर्त पर हुआ है. रिंकू सिंह समेत 8 खिलाड़ी बाहर हैं.
items.body_text:
Sign In
                
                Advertisement
            X
        
        अफगानिस्तान के खिलाफ होने वाली तीन मैचों की टी20 सीरीज के लिए टीम इंडिया का ऐलान कर दिया गया है. श्रेयस अय्यर की कप्तानी में 15 सदस्यीय स्क्वॉड चुनी गई है.
टीम में संजू सैमसन की वापसी हुई है, जबकि युवा बल्लेबाज वैभव सूर्यवंशी को भी जगह मिली है. इस स्क्वॉड में चार खिलाड़ियों का चयन फिटनेस टेस्ट पास करने की शर्त पर हुआ है. जसप्रीत बुमराह, हर्षित राणा, वॉशिंगटन सुंदर और नीतीश कुमार रेड्डी के नाम के साथ स्टार लगा हुआ है.
संजू सैमसन को टी20 टीम में फिर जगह मिली है. वह जिम्बाब्वे दौरे की टीम का हिस्सा नहीं थे. अब अफगानिस्तान के खिलाफ सीरीज में उन्हें विकेटकीपर के तौर पर चुना गया है.
उनके साथ ईशान किशन भी विकेटकीपर के विकल्प हैं. तिलक वर्मा को उपकप्तान बनाया गया है, जबकि श्रेयस अय्यर टीम की कमान संभालेंगे.
India’s squad for Afghanistan T20I series announced. #TeamIndia will play three T20Is against Afghanistan at New Delhi, beginning September 13.#AFGvIND pic.twitter.com/UqTUeZyHz8
— BCCI (@BCCI) September 1, 2026
वैभव सूर्यवंशी का जलवा बरकरार
महज 15 साल के वैभव सूर्यवंशी पर टीम मैनेजमेंट का भरोसा कायम है. उन्हें एक बार फिर टी20 स्क्वॉड में शामिल किया गया है. अभिषेक शर्मा के साथ वैभव टीम के प्रमुख युवा बल्लेबाजी विकल्पों में शामिल हैं.
रिंकू समेत 8 खिलाड़ी बाहर
जिम्बाब्वे दौरे के लिए चुनी गई टीम से तुलना करें तो इस बार 8 खिलाड़ियों को जगह नहीं मिली है. रिंकू सिंह, सूर्यांश शेडगे, हर्ष दुबे, प्रिंस यादव, यश ठाकुर, अशोक शर्मा, मयंक यादव, प्रभसिमरन सिंह शामिल हैं. 
अफगानिस्तान सीरीज के लिए टीम इंडिया का स्कॉड: श्रेयस अय्यर (कप्तान), अभिषेक शर्मा, वैभव सूर्यवंशी, संजू सैमसन (विकेटकीपर), ईशान किशन (विकेटकीपर), तिलक वर्मा (उपकप्तान), शिवम दुबे, नीतीश कुमार रेड्डी*, अक्षर पटेल, वॉशिंगटन सुंदर*, वरुण चक्रवर्ती, रवि बिश्नोई, जसप्रीत बुमराह*, अर्शदीप सिंह और हर्षित राणा*
* फिटनेस के अधीन
भारत के खिलाफ अफगानिस्तान का स्क्वॉड: इब्राहिम जादरान (कप्तान), रहमानुल्लाह गुरबाज (विकेटकीपर), नूर रहमान (विकेटकीपर), सेदिकुल्लाह अटल, दरविश रसूली, अजमतुल्लाह उमरजई, गुलबदीन नायब, मोहम्मद नबी, राशिद खान, नांग्याल खरोटी, नूर अहमद, मुजीब उर रहमान, फजल हक फारूकी, अब्दुल्ला अहमदजई, नवीन-उल-हक
कब होंगे भारत और अफगानिस्तान सीरीज के मुकाबले?
भारत और अफगानिस्तान के बीच तीन टी20 मैचों की सीरीज 13 सितंबर से नई दिल्ली में शुरू होगी. सीरीज के सभी मुकाबले भारत में खेले जाएंगे.
भारत और अफगानिस्तान सीरीज का पूरा शेड्यूल
- पहला टी20-13 सितंबर 2026, अरुण जेटली स्टेडियम (नई दिल्ली)
- दूसरा टी20-15 सितंबर 2026, अरुण जेटली स्टेडियम (नई दिल्ली)
- तीसरा टी20-17 सितंबर 2026, अरुण जेटली स्टेडियम( नई दिल्ली)

items.title: दुनिया को कर्ज बांटने वाले सऊदी अरब को क्या हुआ? क्राउन प्रिंस को चाहिए खरबों का लोन
items.summary: ईरान युद्ध ने सऊदी अरब की कमर तोड़ दी है. तेल से होने वाली कमाई कम हो गई है और प्रिंस सलमान को विजन 2030 पूरा करने के लिए भारी-भरकम कर्ज लेना पड़ रहा है. सऊदी अरब अपनी इकोनॉमी को तेल से हटाकर दूसरे क्षेत्रों में ले जाना चाहता है, इसके लिए उसे अरबों डॉलर खर्च करने पड़ रहे हैं.
items.body_text:
Sign In
                
                Advertisement
            X
        
        सऊदी अरब को भारत में लोग कैसे जानते हैं? अमीर देश, तेल का कुआं, रियाल की करेंसी, पैसा ही पैसा. ऊंची इमारतें, फर्राटा भरती SUV कारें. यानी की ऐसा मुल्क जहां बहुत पैसा है. खबरों में हम देखते-पढ़ते हैं कि सऊदी अरब दुनिया भर में अपना पैसा लगाता है, जिस मुल्क को कर्जे की जरूरत होती है तो सऊदी अरब के पास जाता है. पाकिस्तान को सऊदी अरब परमानेंट फाइनेंशर है.
लेकिन शेखों के मुल्क की तस्वीर इतनी भी गुलाबी नहीं है. सऊदी अरब को अब मोटे कर्जे की जरूरत पड़ गई है. ब्लूमबर्ग की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक सऊदी अरब 8 अरब डॉलर का भारी-भरकम लोन लेने की तैयारी कर रहा है. 8 अरब डॉलर को अगर रुपयों में देखें तो लगभग 7.6 खरब रुपये होते हैं.
दरअसल ईरान युद्ध ने सऊदी अरब की इकोनॉमी पर तगड़ा दवाब डाला है. इस युद्ध के आर्थिक असर के बीच, सऊदी अरब नए लोन से कम से कम 8 अरब डॉलर जुटाने के लिए शुरुआती बातचीत कर रहा है. वह फंडिंग के अलग-अलग सोर्स बनाने की कोशिशें तेज़ कर रहा है.
आइए पूरे मामले को समझते हैं
सऊदी अरब लंबे समय से विश्व का सबसे बड़ा तेल निर्यातक और मध्य पूर्व का वित्तीय महाशक्ति रहा है. सॉवरेन वेल्थ फंड के जरिये सऊदी अरब दुनिया भर में निवेश करता रहा है और विकासशील देशों को सहायता और कर्जे मुहैया कराता रहा है.
सऊदी अरब अब खुद बड़े पैमाने पर ऋण जुटाने की कोशिश में जुटा है. दरअसल क्राउन प्रिंस मोहम्मद बिन सलमान के महात्वाकांक्षी विजन 2030 को फंड करने के लिए सऊदी किंगडम को 'तगड़े लोन' की जरूरत पड़ रही है.
सऊदी अरब का नेशनल डेट मैनेजमेंट सेंटर (NDMC) कम से कम 8 अरब डॉलर के नए सिंडिकेटेड लोन के लिए बैंकों से बातचीत कर रहा है. सऊदी की सरकारी तेल कंपनी अरामको भी इसी तरह के फाइनेंसिंग विकल्पों पर चर्चा कर रही है.
ईरान युद्ध से तगड़ा नुकसान
सऊदी अरब को पैसे की जरूरत इसलिए पैदा हुई क्योंकि क्षेत्रीय युद्ध (ईरान से जुड़े संघर्ष) ने तेल निर्यात, व्यापार मार्गों (खासकर होर्मुज स्ट्रेट ) और सप्लाई चेन पर दबाव डाला है. इसकी वजह से सऊदी का निर्यात कम हुआ है.
तेहरान ने सऊदी अरब के एनर्जी इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर को निशाना बनाया है, जबकि ईरान समर्थित हूती विद्रोहियों ने लाल सागर में जहाजों के लिए खतरा पैदा कर दिया है. स्ट्रेट ऑफ होर्मुज बंद होने से सऊदी तेल की ब्रिकी कम हो गई है, जबकि हूती विद्रोहियों की वजह से बाब अल मंदेब भी बंद रहता है.
इस बीच कोरोना महामारी के बाद से दूसरी तिमाही में सऊदी अर्थव्यवस्था में सबसे बड़ी गिरावट देखी गई; इन हमलों की वजह से तेल सेक्टर में लगभग 25% की गिरावट आई. यहां बताना चाहेंगे कि सऊदी अरब की कमाई का सबसे बड़ा स्रोत कच्चे तेल की बिक्री ही है.
हालांकि कच्चे तल की कीमतों में इजाफा होने से सऊदी को कुछ राहत भी मिली है.
इससे पहले 2025 के अंत में NDMC ने 13 अरब डॉलर का सात साल का सिंडिकेटेड लोन जुटाया था, जो बिजली, पानी और सार्वजनिक उपयोगिता परियोजनाओं के लिए था.
2026 की वार्षिक उधार योजना में वित्त मंत्रालय ने लगभग 58 अरब डॉलर की कुल फाइनेंसिंग जरूरत बताई है. यानी सऊदी को इतना पैसा चाहिए. इसमें करीब 44 अरब डॉलर का बजट घाटा और 14 अरब डॉलर के कर्ज से हासिल करना शामिल है.
सऊदी अरब को इतना पैसा चाहिए क्यों?
सऊदी अरब को इतने हैवी पैसे की जरूरत की वजह उसका विजन 2030 है. 2016 में एमबीएस द्वारा शुरू की गई इस योजना का लक्ष्य तेल निर्भरता कम करके पर्यटन, मनोरंजन, मैन्युफैक्चरिंग, लॉजिस्टिक्स और प्रौद्योगिकी क्षेत्रों में अर्थव्यवस्था को कई क्षेत्रों में ले जाना है. क्राउन प्रिंस सलमान नहीं चाहते हैं कि जब सऊदी का कच्चा तेल खत्म हो जाए तो उसे अचानक आर्थिक तकलीफों का सामना करना पड़े. इसलिए सलमान समय रहते ही सऊदी की अर्थव्यवस्था को और क्षेत्रों के लिए खोलना चाहते हैं.
इस प्रोजेक्ट को लेकर वे इतने जुनूनी है कि उन्होंने कहा था कि 'दुनिया में कोई ताकत विजन 2030 को विफल नहीं कर सकती.'
इस प्रोजेक्ट के तहत ही सलमान नेओम, रेड सी प्रोजेक्ट, क़िद्दिया जैसे गिगा-प्रोजेक्ट्स पर सैकड़ों अरब डॉलर खर्च कर रे हैं. इसमें कुल निवेश की जरूरत एक ट्रिलियन डॉलर से ज्यादा आंकी गई है. लेकिन तेल कीमतों में उतार-चढ़ाव और उत्पादन कटौती ने सऊदी की कमाई को प्रभावित किया है. 2026 की पहली तिमाही में बजट घाटा 33.5 अरब डॉलर तक पहुंच गया.
सऊदी सुरक्षा के मोर्चे पर भी भारी भरकम निवेश कर रहा है. 2024 में सऊदी अरब का रक्षा बजट लगभग 75.8 अरब अमेरिकी डॉलर रहा, जबकि 2025 में ये रकम लगभग 78 अरब अमेरिकी डॉलर थी. यह कुल सरकारी खर्चे का करीब 21% और GDP का लगभग 7.1% था.
