items.title: Police nominate three accused in Abdullah Tahir murder case
items.summary: Police nominate three accused in Abdullah Tahir murder case
items.body_text:
Police nominate three accused in Abdullah Tahir murder case
- By Yar Muhammad -
- Sep 01, 2026
LAHORE: Police has nominated three accused in murder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Chaudhry Abdullah Tahir in Lahore.
Tiktoker Laraib and Abdullah Tahir’s driver, Asghar, have been nominated in the murder case. Laraib and Asghar have been charged of facilitation by sharing location of the murder victim with killers.
The accused involved in reconnaissance of the PTI leader has also been named in the case, police said.
Police have so far detained five people on suspicion including the tiktoker.
Main shooter Arsalan and two other gunmen have not been arrested so far.
The interior ministry has issued red warrants of Gogi Butt, who has been charged of conspiring killing of Abdullah Tahir with contract killers.
Police investigating the murder earlier suggested that the killing was meticulously planned.
Police sources earlier said the arrested suspects told investigators that the murder was carried out after extensive planning. They revealed that drones were used to monitor Abdullah Tahir’s movements and identify his location before the attack.
Investigators said a significant amount of money was spent to arrange the drone surveillance. Police are also examining reports of drone activity in the vicinity of the victim’s residence before the murder.
PTI leader from Okara, Chaudhry Abdullah Tahir was killed in a gun attack during his visit to a clinic for routine check up on July 29.
According to police, two motorcycle-riding gunmen opened indiscriminate fire on Abdullah Tahir in Lahore’s Gulberg area. He suffered multiple gunshot wounds and later succumbed to his injuries.
Abdullah Tahir was a prominent political figure from Okara and had contested the 2018 Punjab Assembly elections on a PTI ticket.

items.title: Pakistan’s inflation rises to 11.15% in August 2026
items.summary: Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose to 8.7% year-over-year in August, up from 8.4% in July. The post Pakistan’s inflation rises to 11.15% in August 2026 appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
Pakistan’s inflation rises to 11.15% in August 2026
Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose to 8.7% year-over-year in August, up from 8.4% in July.
Web Desk
KARACHI: Pakistan’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation climbed to 11.15% year-over-year in August 2026, up 1.19% from the previous month, matching analysts’ projections of 11.09%.
The annual increase was driven largely by a 13.89% rise in food prices, a 20.17% jump in transport costs and a 13.6% increase in communication expenses, according to the data.
On a monthly basis, transport was the largest contributor to inflation, rising 3.41%, followed by a 1.66% increase in food prices.
Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose to 8.7% year-over-year in August, up from 8.4% in July.
The transport segment posted a 3.41% monthly increase and a 20% annual rise, reflecting higher fuel prices tied to increased international oil costs. Motor fuel prices alone rose 5.61% during the month.
Food inflation reached 1.66% on a monthly basis, driven primarily by sharp price increases for onions, which rose 46%, and eggs, up 12%.
The Housing, Water, Electricity and Gas category recorded inflation of 0.55%. Within the segment, liquefied petroleum gas prices fell 1.31% month-over-month, but the decline was offset by a 1.7% rise in electricity charges.
The increase in electricity costs was mainly attributed to a higher Fuel Charges Adjustment, which rose to Rs0.7503 per kilowatt-hour from Rs0.3364 per kilowatt-hour in July. Water costs also rose 4.15%, adding further pressure to the segment.
With headline inflation at 11.2% for August, Pakistan’s real interest rate stood at 0.4%, slightly above the country’s historic average range of 200 to 300 basis points.

items.title: Google Messages bug resurfaces old texts in new conversations, sparks privacy concerns

items.body_text:
Google Messages bug resurfaces old texts in new conversations, sparks privacy concerns
The reports have raised concerns because the bug can potentially place private or sensitive messages alongside new conversations.
Web Desk
Google Messages users are reporting a troubling bug in which old messages from unrelated conversations appear alongside new texts, images or group messages, raising privacy concerns for phone owners.
The issue has been reported in multiple threads. Users say the problem occurs when they start a new conversation, but the Messages app displays an old message from another chat next to the new content.
In some cases, the problem goes beyond what appears on the screen. Users have reported that an old message can be attached to a new message and delivered to the wrong person.
Other reports mention verification codes and private messages being attached to new conversations and sent to unintended recipients. Users say the issue has affected both Pixel and Samsung phones.
The problem also appears to occur regardless of whether Rich Communication Services (RCS), is turned on or off. Several users have tried common troubleshooting steps without success. These include clearing the Google Messages app cache, restarting the phone, turning RCS off and back on, and reinstalling the app.
Some users have claimed that a full factory reset stopped the problem. However, they said this worked only when they did not restore previous message backups.
There is no indication in the information provided that Google has confirmed either method as a reliable fix. A factory reset can also remove data from a device, making a backup important before taking such a step.
Google has acknowledged the issue at least once. The company asked a user who reported the bug to provide screenshots and submit feedback through the Messages app.
The reports have raised concerns because the bug can potentially place private or sensitive messages alongside new conversations. For now, users reporting the issue have not identified a consistent solution that works for everyone.

items.title: Tim Cook steps down as Apple CEO after 15 years
items.summary: Tim Cook moves to executive chairman as John Ternus takes the CEO role, putting Apple under new leadership at a crucial moment for artificial intelligence. The post Tim Cook steps down as Apple CEO after 15 years appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
CUPERTINO: After 15 years at Apple’s helm, Tim Cook is handing the reins to John Ternus on Tuesday, opening a new chapter for the technology giant as it confronts the next wave of artificial intelligence and product innovation. Cook will remain at Apple as executive chairman.
Cook formally stepped down as CEO after leading Apple since 2011, when he succeeded co-founder Steve Jobs. Ternus, Apple’s senior vice president of Hardware Engineering, officially takes over as CEO on Sept. 1, marking Apple’s first CEO transition in 15 years.
The transition closes one of the most consequential leadership chapters in Apple’s history. Under Cook, the company grew from a roughly $350 billion enterprise into a technology powerhouse valued at more than $4 trillion, while expanding beyond its hardware business into services and other areas.
Cook’s final message
On his final day as CEO, Cook sent a message to Apple employees reflecting on his time at the company and expressing gratitude to the people who helped shape its growth.
“Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO,” Cook wrote in a post on X, formerly known as Twitter. “My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will.”
Cook said Apple’s achievements were ultimately the result of its people and emphasized that the accomplishments he valued most could not necessarily be measured in an annual report.

He also expressed confidence in Ternus and said he was comfortable handing the company’s leadership to an executive he considers highly capable.
Although Cook is leaving the CEO position, he is not leaving Apple.
He will serve as executive chairman of the company’s board, allowing him to remain involved with Apple while Ternus takes responsibility for its day-to-day operations. Apple announced the leadership transition in April following a succession process approved unanimously by its board.
“As you know, I am not leaving Apple,” Cook wrote. “But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply.”
Cook said he would miss leading the company and working alongside employees but added that he was at peace with the decision.
He also praised Ternus, describing him as “brilliant,” “wonderful” and capable of leading Apple into its next phase.
Who is John Ternus?
Ternus joined Apple in 2001 and has spent more than two decades working on the company’s hardware operations. He became senior vice president of Hardware Engineering in 2021 and has played a major role in the development of Apple’s hardware products.
His promotion puts a hardware-focused executive in charge at a time when Apple is under growing pressure to accelerate its artificial intelligence strategy.
Ternus inherits a company with an enormous global customer base, a powerful ecosystem and a vast services business, but also one facing intense competition from technology companies moving quickly in AI.
The challenges ahead
One of Ternus’ biggest challenges will be keeping Apple competitive in artificial intelligence.
Apple has faced criticism over delays in its AI development, particularly the rollout of a more advanced Siri. The company has increasingly relied on partnerships and outside technology as it works to strengthen its AI capabilities.
Apple also faces questions surrounding some of its newer products. Its Vision Pro mixed-reality headset has struggled to achieve the level of commercial success the company hoped for, while reports of layoffs and restructuring in the Vision Pro division have added to concerns about the platform’s future.
The company has also abandoned its long-running electric vehicle project, another example of the difficulty Apple has faced when expanding into entirely new product categories.

items.body_text:
Iraq weighs oil-backed U.S. bank loan to tackle liquidity shortfall
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi government is preparing to formally engage official U.S. banking institutions to secure an emergency sovereign loan facility backed by future crude oil export revenues, an informed official source disclosed to local news agencies.
The financing initiative is designed as a rapid intervention to bridge expanding state cash-flow deficits and secure public sector payroll obligations without resorting to domestic currency printing.
Financing Structure & Diplomatic Coordination
- Inter-Ministerial Formulation: The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are coordinating the joint terms of engagement to present formal loan requests to designated American banking institutions.
- Oil Revenue Collateral: Debt-service installments and loan principal repayments are structured to be settled directly from Iraq’s international crude sales proceeds in global energy markets.
- Inflation Prevention Policy: Securing foreign currency credit provides an alternative to unbacked domestic monetary expansion, mitigating risks of dinar devaluation and consumer price inflation.
Emergency Legislative Framework
To implement the credit facility, the executive branch is finalizing specialized fiscal legislation for parliamentary ratification:
- Draft Borrowing Law: The proposed Borrowing, Grants, and Subsidies Law serves as a statutory spending bridge to sustain vital state operations in the absence of a comprehensive annual budget framework.
- Parliamentary Finance Committee Review: Lawmakers are awaiting the official submission of the cabinet’s draft bill to establish clear spending ceilings, debt sustainability parameters, and compliance with national fiscal targets.
Key Macroeconomic & Monetary Indicators
The decision to pursue external commercial borrowing underscores Baghdad’s focus on maintaining monetary discipline amid regional geopolitical volatility and oil price fluctuations.
By utilizing structured sovereign credit instead of domestic quantitative easing, the Ministry of Finance aims to preserve liquidity reserves, meet mandatory salary disbursements on schedule, and protect the exchange value of the Iraqi Dinar.

items.body_text:
Iraq ranks 61st globally in PPP minimum wage at $626: Report
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq ranks 61st globally out of 130 countries in monthly minimum wage adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), recording $626 per month, according to an international comparative index published by Visual Capitalist.
The ranking adjusts statutory wage baselines to account for local price levels, subsidized consumer baskets, and relative costs of living across economies, providing an accurate metric of real purchasing capacity rather than nominal dollar conversions.
Global and Regional Comparative Standings
Iraq placed in the upper-middle tier of the 130-nation survey, closely outpacing emerging and regional economies:
- Adjacent Global Peers: Iraq ($626/mo) marginally led South Africa (62nd at $620/mo) and Guyana (63rd at $619/mo).
- Regional & Major Economy Comparisons: Iraq recorded higher real purchasing capacity at the baseline wage floor than China (73rd at $544/mo) and Tunisia (77th at $513/mo).
- Global Leaders:Switzerland led the index with a PPP-adjusted minimum wage of $3,804 per month, followed by Germany, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, while the United States ranked 25th at $1,257 per month.
- Lower-Tier Rankings: Developing economies at the base of the index included Niger (121st at $196/mo), Ghana (127th at $100/mo), and Gambia (130th at $67/mo).
Global Minimum Wage Rankings (PPP-Adjusted Monthly USD)
The $626 PPP valuation reflects how local price subsidies, utility price caps, and domestic living costs expand the real-term domestic purchasing capacity of Iraq’s statutory minimum wage (nominally set at 350,000 IQD per month by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs).
While nominal conversion rates place Iraq’s minimum wage near $268 USD, purchasing power adjustments demonstrate that baseline earners retain greater domestic absorption capacity than several larger industrial peers where basic living expenses and utility tariffs are considerably higher.

items.body_text:
Vice President JD Vance said in Michigan on Monday that “there’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very, evil,” arguing that the state’s Democratic Senate nominee is symptomatic of a growing trend in America of fighting “for one group at the expense of others.”
His sharp criticism of El-Sayed — which included telling the Democrat to “keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth” — underscored how heated the rhetoric has become in this competitive Senate race, which could be critical in the larger battle for control of the chamber.
Vance cast the choice between El-Sayed and GOP nominee Mike Rogers as about who would fight for all Michiganders — even if they don’t agree 100% with Rogers — while obliquely suggesting that El-Sayed cared more about members of the Muslim community than other voters.
“There’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very evil and on the rise in the United States of America today, and it’s people who see themselves not as citizens of a common nation, fighting for every single person … but see themselves as fighting for one group at the expense of others,” Vance said at a rally in Sterling Heights hosted by MAGA Inc., a super PAC aligned with President Donald Trump.
“What I see is a man who has sympathy and compassion for people who share his religion, but have nothing for people who don’t. A person who will apologize for a murderer so long as he looks the right way, but will not understand the plight of an innocent child if that person has the wrong faith,” Vance said, calling on voters to “reject it in November” and back Rogers.
El-Sayed on Monday pushed back on Vance’s comments, casting the Trump administration and Republicans as the ones perpetrating evil.
“Evil is ripping healthcare away from working people in exchange for tax breaks for billionaires. Evil is making people pay more for groceries and gas while pushing for trade wars and actual war. Evil is dividing people for your own gain. Evil is selling out your morals for a little bit of power,” he said in a statement.
“Michigan is better than being lectured to by sock puppets from Ohio and Florida. We understand what’s at stake, and Michiganders will show you at the ballot box this November when we send Mike Rogers packing,” he added.
El-Sayed recently apologized for saying after a March attack on a Michigan synagogue that “violence is a cycle” and that “hurt people hurt people.” (The attacker lost family in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon a week before the Michigan attack.) At the time, El-Sayed also condemned the synagogue attack and antisemitism broadly.
Vance’s speech became more personal as he took aim at recent comments from El-Sayed that some viewed as racist. Earlier this month, the Democratic candidate responded to a clip of Vance at a rally referencing his late grandfather, “Papaw,” by mentioning second lady Usha Vance, who is the child of Indian immigrants and was raised Hindu.
“So do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no…” El-Sayed wrote on X.
“I’d rather not talk about spouses at all,” El-Sayed told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Monday evening on “The Source,” as he sought to clarify his comment about the vice president’s wife. “The point that I’ve been making about his wife is that he believes in a political philosophy that says that some people are somehow more American than others.”
Vance on Monday said El-Sayed has a “weird habit of talking about my family,” going on to lob a series of misleading claims at the Democrat — a pattern that’s emerged from the GOP since El-Sayed won the Senate nomination in early August, with some Republicans resorting to overtly Islamophobic attacks.
“My message to Abdul El-Sayed is: You can pal around with terrorist sympathizers, and you can say that America deserved 9/11, or you could empathize not with the children who were targeted at Temple Israel, but with the attacker,” Vance said.

items.title: Rashwan: Accurate, timely information vital to combating rumors
items.summary: Egypt’s Minister of State for Information Diaa Rashwan emphasized the vital importance of coordination among government spokespersons, media advisers, and print, broadcast and television media outlets to ensure the rapid flow of accurate information on state and community affairs. He said providing official accounts of events, decisions, measures and achievements would help close information gaps … The post Rashwan: Accurate, timely information vital to combating rumors appeared first on Egypt I
items.body_text:
Egypt’s Minister of State for Information Diaa Rashwan emphasized the vital importance of coordination among government spokespersons, media advisers, and print, broadcast and television media outlets to ensure the rapid flow of accurate information on state and community affairs.
He said providing official accounts of events, decisions, measures and achievements would help close information gaps and prevent the spread of rumors and false reports aimed at undermining state efforts and social stability.
Speaking at an expanded meeting attended by 35 government spokespersons and media advisers, Rashwan said improving their performance was part of presidential directives to enhance Egyptian media and strengthen its role in raising public awareness and positively influencing public opinion.
This requires government officials to provide information promptly and respond to media requests in order to present the facts and the views of state institutions, he added.
Rashwan also pointed to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s repeated calls for opening up the public sphere and allowing space for different opinions on issues and topics within the framework of the Constitution, the law and national interests.
Participants highlighted several challenges, including the spread of inaccurate information and fabricated reports on social media, as well as the reliance of some media outlets on social media as a source of information.
They also raised concerns that some newspapers and websites do not give sufficient attention to information provided by official sources.
The participants called for a clear definition of the roles and responsibilities of government spokespersons and media advisers, greater access to information within their institutions, and advanced training programs for spokespersons, media advisers, journalists and media professionals covering ministries and government institutions.
Rashwan said developing the performance of government spokespersons and media advisers was among the ministry’s main priorities and that training programs for various segments of the media sector were currently being prepared.
He added that the ministry would coordinate with government bodies and media organizations to establish clear mechanisms for continued cooperation and ensure the timely and adequate flow of information.

Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad discussed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, a number of projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.
She also stressed the need for regular follow-up of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards, along with establishing a continuous environmental monitoring plan.
The remarks came during the 76th meeting of the board of directors of the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) which discussed a number of issues related to developing the environmental work system, supporting environmental projects and investment, maximizing the sustainable utilization of natural resources and following up on the implementation of decisions and recommendations issued at previous board meetings. These efforts aim to enhance institutional performance and support the state’s efforts to protect the environment and improve citizens’ quality of life.
The meeting was attended by CEO of the EEAA Sherif Abdel Rahim as well as representatives of the ministries of defense, industry, foreign affairs and international cooperation, planning and economic development, water resources and irrigation, health and higher education and scientific research in addition to a number of environmental experts and officials from the ministry of local development and environment.
At the beginning of the meeting, Awad affirmed the ministry’s commitment to continuing to develop the environmental work system and improve performance, as well as supporting projects that contribute to environmental protection and the preservation of natural resources.
She stressed the importance of coordination and integration among all relevant authorities and accelerating the implementation of environmental policies and programs to ensure that plans are translated into tangible results on the ground.
She explained that the board began its session by approving the minutes of meeting No. 74 and reviewing the implementation status of the decisions and recommendations issued by it, as well as the implementation status of the decisions of meeting No. 75.
This reflects the ministry’s commitment to continuously monitoring implementation rates and enhancing institutional efficiency.
Awad also pointed out that, as part of the state’s drive to promote environmental investment and encourage the private sector to participate in developing natural destinations, the board discussed several projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.
The board reviewed the technical and financial assessments, permit durations and technical and financial proposals concerning several applications submitted by companies seeking to invest in nature reserves, while preserving their geological and environmental characteristics.
Awad further stressed the need for regular monitoring of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards.
She called for a continuous environmental monitoring plan, environmental awareness programs and measures to encourage visitors to adopt sustainable practices, while ensuring that environmental impact assessment studies are conducted and coordination is maintained with the EEAA and relevant authorities to safeguard biodiversity and ensure the sustainability of reserve resources.

Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

Once bitter enemies Amhara, Tigray reach understandings in fight against Ethiopian govt          
        In mid-August, the leader of the Amhara insurgency fighting to overthrow Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed made a surprising announcement.
The collection of armed Amhara movements fighting in the country’s northwest under the unified Fano umbrella would join an alliance of seven other anti-government groups across the country, Fano leader Zemene Kassie told the Swiss publication, Le Temps.
What makes the move surprising is that the alliance includes members of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), whom the Amhara forces that make up the Fano fought against during the 2020-2022 war.
In addition to the TPLF, the alliance includes forces from Gumuz, Oromo, the Berta people and Somalia, Zemene said.
At the national level, the fight between Ethiopian oppositional groups and the government comes against the backdrop of a struggle over the future of the country’s multinational federal system and state’s right to self-determination.
However, this tension has a larger regional dynamic given Ethiopia’s involvement in the war in Sudan and its expressed desire to secure access to the Red Sea either by diplomatic coup or by force.
While fighting between the Fano and the Ethiopian government has transformed much of the Amhara Region into an active war zone since late 2023, the beginning of August saw clashes between TPLF forces and the Ethiopian military that threatened to transform long standing simmering tensions between the groups into an active war.
An African Union diplomat based in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr at the time that any expansion of the fighting in Tigray would have an impact on the calculations of every regional actor because the borders linking Sudan, Ethiopia and Eritrea are no longer merely dividing lines between states. They now form part of an interconnected regional security system in which domestic wars and geopolitical interests overlap, the diplomat added, making any new outbreak of fighting in Tigray a potential factor in reshaping the security landscape of the entire East African region.
The government has responded to the early August clashes with increased military activity.
In a statement issued on Friday, the Tigray regional government warned the international community that the region is nearing “another catastrophic war.”
An economic and security blockade has escalated following clashes that broke out on August 1, the statement added, with air strikes and artillery shelling hitting civilian areas, causing casualties and destruction and disrupting cultural activities.
In an interview with Oromia Broadcasting Network on August 7, Abiy criticized the TPLF leadership, accusing it of clinging to outdated political methods and forging alliances that he said threaten stability.
TPLF deputy chair Amanuel Assefa pointed to a strike on August 20, when a drone hit a residential area in Mekelle, Tigray’s capital. Residents speaking to Mada Masr confirmed the strike and said several homes were damaged.
Medical sources at Mekelle’s Ayder Specialized Hospital said 13 people were brought in with injuries following the strike, including five women and children, with three in serious condition. The injured ranged in age from two to 60, the sources said.
Tigrayan authorities also said a second strike hit near Mekelle University, though there is no confirmed information on casualties or damage as of the time of publishing.
The strike on Mekelle came only days after another attack that Tigrayan authorities attributed to the Ethiopian military, where a drone struck a farmers’ training center in the Dandera village, about 15 km from Mekelle, on August 18.
While the government hit Tigray, Fano forces continued to secure strategic wins against the Ethiopian military.

items.body_text:
Warraq residents demonstrate to protest ‘state ignoring legitimate demands’          
        Hundreds of Warraq Island residents held a protest march on Tuesday, after the head of the authority tasked with developing the island failed to respond to demands they submitted last week, one of the participants in the march told Mada Masr.
Hundreds of residents gathered in the street on Tuesday morning, on the deadline they had given authorities to respond to demands they submitted last week, including that they be granted lands within the state development project, according to the participant as well as videos published by other residents who attended the march.
The crowd then marched toward the New Warraq City Development headquarters, where a heavy security deployment awaited them. Security officials told them that the head of the authority asked for a small group to enter for negotiations.
The protestors refused, instead demanding that the authority’s head come down to meet them, in an attempt to get a direct response to the demands they had already submitted in writing.
The resident who took part in Tuesday’s march said the authority head’s refusal to come down and meet the residents sparked anger among many of them, but that they kept it in check out of their keenness to keep the protest peaceful.
But it showed “a lack of consideration, especially since he didn’t meet us when we came to hand over the demands,” the resident said.
The same sentiment was clear at the protest. “Nobody has paid us any attention,” one of the protesters called out to the assembled crowd. “At this moment, we register our objection to the state’s disregard for our legitimate and just demands by saying just one thing: God is sufficient for us, and he is the best disposer of all affairs,” indicating the group’s loss of faith in the authorities’ seriousness.
The residents then continued their peaceful protest march along the route that had been agreed to in advance. While the march had been planned without chants, still, the residents raised similar cries of “God is sufficient for us” and “one hand.”
At the end of the march, the residents agreed to meet again on Friday to discuss their next steps, and raised the possibility of disrupting ongoing development work on the island.
The residents had submitted a list of demands to the authority on August 18, foremost among them that they be allocated a plot of land within the island’s redevelopment area, where residents who have chosen to stay could build their own homes, according to a defined timeline, with clear and specific implementation mechanisms and fair conditions. They also put forward other demands concerning living and security conditions on the island.
The group handed their written demands to the authority’s deputy chair at the time, with the head elsewhere with another group of Warraq residents, inspecting one of the island’s schools, supposedly to assess potential upgrades.
The resident described to Mada Masr the authority head’s meeting with that group as part of security attempts to “divide.”
One of the people in the group that did not join Tuesday’s march said there were some who had not attended the recent meeting that produced the list of demands. The group who went with the authority head on his school visit opposes holding marches to the authority’s offices, they told Mada Masr. Instead, they have been trying to communicate with officials at the authority and pressure them to implement “as many things as possible that would allow us to keep living on the island,” they continued, adding that they are convinced the government would not agree to give residents land on the island to replace their homes.
The source pointed to what they saw as officials responding to some of the residents’ service-related demands, including bringing back sewage pumping trucks and beginning to clear demolition waste that had piled up along the island’s roads.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly held a meeting at the government headquarters in the New Administrative Capital on Monday to review the final arrangements for an upcoming visit to Egypt by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
 
The meeting was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, Presidential Advisor for Economic Affairs Hala El-Said, and Presidential Advisor for Financial Affairs Ahmed El-Shazly. Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk participated via video conference alongside other relevant officials.
“We have previously held a number of meetings to prepare for the Chinese president’s visit to Egypt, and today we are finalising the arrangements for this important visit,” Madbouly stated at the beginning of the meeting.
The prime minister emphasised the significance of the Chinese President visit in expanding cooperation frameworks and advancing joint coordination across various fields.The prime minister emphasised the significance of the Chinese President visit in expanding cooperation frameworks and advancing joint coordination across various fields. Madbouly highlighted the role of the Cabinet’s special China Unit in deepening cooperation in diverse developmental and economic areas and exploring potential projects for future collaboration under the two nations’ comprehensive strategic partnership.
Madbouly highlighted the role of the Cabinet’s special China Unit in deepening cooperation in diverse developmental and economic areas and exploring potential projects for future collaboration under the two nations’ comprehensive strategic partnership.
 
During the meeting, officials reviewed existing joint projects and stressed the importance of building on tangible progress achieved in bilateral relations. Attendees highlighted the need to enhance investment opportunities, noting confidence within the Chinese business community in the Egyptian investment climate and calling for deeper cooperation in priority sectors.
 
The upcoming visit comes as Cairo and Beijing mark seven decades since the establishment of diplomatic relations. Over the past 70 years, bilateral ties have been maintained on principles of national independence, respect for sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, and the right of nations to choose their own political and developmental paths.
China’s developmental model presents an approach for developing countries across Africa and the Arab world, demonstrating that progress can emerge from a society’s specific culture, resources, and national priorities rather than an imported template. Geographically positioned at the intersection of the Middle East, Africa, and the Arab world, Egypt serves as a strategic meeting point connecting China with the broader African continent and Arab region.

items.summary: Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Hussein Issa arrived in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek on Monday to participate in the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, representing President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi. Issa was received upon arrival by the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic, Sitek Jumakadyrovich Jumakadyr uulu, and the […] The post Egypt’s deputy PM joins global leaders in Bishkek for 25th anniversary SCO summit first appeared on Dailynewsegyp
items.body_text:
Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Hussein Issa arrived in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek on Monday to participate in the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, representing President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.
Issa was received upon arrival by the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic, Sitek Jumakadyrovich Jumakadyr uulu, and the Chargé d’Affaires of the Egyptian Mission to the Republics of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, Ibrahim Hamza.
The deputy prime minister is scheduled to deliver Egypt’s address at the two-day summit and hold a series of high-level bilateral meetings with officials from participating countries and representatives of international organisations.
The summit, which kicked off on Monday under the motto “Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity”, marks the 25th anniversary of the SCO’s establishment. The gathering convenes at a time when the world is grappling with the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war and the aftermath of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, which has upended global energy and financial markets.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi have arrived in Bishkek for the summit, alongside Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. On the sidelines of the event, Xi held a meeting with Putin.
The summit is also attended by the leaders of Pakistan, Uzbekistan, Belarus, and Kazakhstan. Furthermore, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn are expected to attend.
The SCO started in 1996 as a security bloc dubbed the “Shanghai Five”, formed by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan to settle border disputes following the end of the Cold War and the collapse of the Soviet Union.
In June 2001, the Beijing-headquartered grouping evolved into the SCO, expanding to include Uzbekistan. The bloc expanded again to include India and Pakistan in 2017, followed by Iran and Belarus as full members in 2023 and 2024, respectively. In addition to its full members, the organisation has 14 key dialogue partners, including Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkiye, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, and Cambodia.

items.body_text:
India is set to make a significant appearance at the El Alamein International Airshow 2026, with the Indian Air Force’s Sarang Helicopter Display Team showcasing the country’s growing indigenous aerospace and defence capabilities in Egypt.
The airshow will take place from 8-10 September at El Alamein International Airport, bringing together international aerospace and defence companies, military delegations and aviation enthusiasts.
Sarang will perform using India’s Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Dhruv, offering audiences a demonstration of one of the country’s key domestically developed helicopter platforms.
India’s participation comes as the country continues to expand domestic defence manufacturing under its “Self-Reliant India” strategy. Domestic production now meets around 65% of India’s annual defence equipment requirements, while Indian defence products are exported to more than 80 countries.
The country has developed capabilities across a wide range of defence sectors, including fighter aircraft, helicopters, warships, submarines, missiles, artillery, air-defence systems, radars, electronic warfare, drones and counter-drone technologies.
India’s defence transformation has also been accompanied by a growing role for private companies and start-ups. Private-sector firms account for approximately 24% of total defence production, while more than 2,000 defence start-ups are developing technologies in areas such as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, drone swarms, robotics, electronic warfare, advanced sensors, secure communications and quantum technologies.
Indian participation at El Alamein also comes against the backdrop of expanding defence ties between India and Egypt, which have developed over more than six decades through military training, institutional exchanges, joint exercises and high-level defence engagements.
In December 2025, India’s Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, visited Egypt at the invitation of the Commander of the Egyptian Air Force. The 11th meeting of the India-Egypt Joint Defence Committee was subsequently held in Cairo in April 2026, where the two sides agreed on a Defence Cooperation Plan for 2026-27.
Military cooperation has continued to expand through exercises. India deployed more than 700 personnel from its Army, Navy and Air Force for Egypt’s multinational Exercise Bright Star in 2025, marking its largest-ever participation in the exercise.
The two countries have also strengthened Special Forces cooperation through Exercise Cyclone, whose fourth edition was held in Cairo in April 2026.
Beyond the airshow, India’s expanding defence industry could create opportunities for deeper industrial cooperation with Egypt in areas including helicopters and aerospace, drones and counter-drone systems, air defence, electronic warfare, maritime surveillance, autonomous systems, sensors, secure communications, and maintenance, repair and overhaul.
The Indian presence at El Alamein is therefore expected to serve as both an aviation showcase and an opportunity to highlight the growing depth of India-Egypt defence relations, while opening further avenues for cooperation in defence production, technology and aerospace.

items.title: More Than 177,000 Syrians Remain Forcibly Disappeared Since 2011, Rights Group Says
items.summary: The Syrian Network for Human Rights says the fall of the Assad regime has not closed one of Syria’s gravest files, calling for a nationwide effort to locate the missing, preserve evidence and hold perpetrators accountable. The post More Than 177,000 Syrians Remain Forcibly Disappeared Since 2011, Rights Group Says first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
The Syrian Network for Human Rights says the fall of the Assad regime has not closed one of Syria’s gravest files, calling for a nationwide effort to locate the missing, preserve evidence and hold perpetrators accountable.
More than 177,000 people remain forcibly disappeared in Syria more than fifteen years after the start of the conflict, according to the Syrian Network for Human Rights, which warned that determining their fate has become an urgent test for the country’s transitional justice process.
In its annual report marking the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances, the rights group said at least 177,021 people, including 4,536 children and 8,984 women, have remained forcibly disappeared since March 2011.
The report, Fifteen Years of Enforced Disappearance in Syria: Families’ Right to the Truth Remains an Ongoing Obligation, also documented the deaths of at least 45,365 people as a result of torture or inhumane detention conditions over the same period. Of those, 45,038 died in detention facilities run by the former Assad regime.
The network stressed that its figures represent minimum estimates, meaning the true scale of enforced disappearance and deaths in detention is likely to be significantly higher than the number of cases it has been able to document.
The organisation described enforced disappearance as one of the central instruments of repression employed by the Assad government following the outbreak of protests in 2011. Arbitrary detention and disappearance were carried out on a wide scale against protesters and individuals regarded as actual or suspected opponents of the government.
The detention system was accompanied by torture, sexual violence, denial of medical care, unlawful killings and deaths caused by inhumane conditions, while families were systematically denied reliable information about the fate and whereabouts of detainees.
The network also documented serious abuses by other parties to the Syrian conflict, including cases that met the legal criteria for enforced disappearance, as well as arbitrary detention, abduction and hostage-taking. It nevertheless emphasised substantial differences in the scale, patterns and attribution of violations committed by the former Assad regime and those committed by other actors.
Regime’s fall leaves disappearance cases unresolved
The overthrow of the Assad government on 8 December 2024 did not end the disappearance crisis, the network said. Under international law, enforced disappearance is considered a continuing violation for as long as the fate or whereabouts of the missing person remain unknown.
Syria must therefore move from a period dominated by documentation, much of it conducted under severe restrictions, towards systematic efforts to determine the fate of the missing. That process should include securing former detention sites, protecting evidence, locating and documenting mass graves, examining government archives and connecting databases and sources of information that were previously fragmented.
The issue presents both a humanitarian and judicial challenge for Syria’s new authorities. Thousands of families have spent more than a decade without knowing whether relatives are alive or dead. Many have been unable to hold funerals, obtain reliable death certificates, settle inheritance cases or resolve other legal and civil matters.
The network said the definition of a victim should extend beyond the disappeared person to include relatives and others who suffered direct harm as a result of the disappearance. It called for families to be placed at the centre of all efforts to locate the missing and for any system established to provide transparency while maintaining confidentiality and protecting personal data. Particular consideration should be given to women, children and other groups facing heightened vulnerability.

items.title: Suweida Students Barred from Exams; UN Urges Protection of Their Right to Education
items.summary: The Suweida Media Directorate announced that the exams were postponed to 11:00 AM to ensure students’ safety and secure their arrival The post Suweida Students Barred from Exams; UN Urges Protection of Their Right to Education first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Students in Suweida were prevented from leaving the city on Saturday morning to reach designated exam centers for the exceptional makeup session of the basic and general secondary education certificates, after groups described by the governorate as “outlaws” blocked their movement. The obstruction delayed the start of the exams, which eventually proceeded in centers across the northern countryside.
The Suweida Media Directorate announced that the exams were postponed to 11:00 AM to ensure students’ safety and secure their arrival. It confirmed that the delay resulted from the actions of the groups that barred students from leaving the city.
Suweida Governor Mustafa Al-Bakour said the blockade triggered frustration among students and their families, escalating into physical altercations and vandalism of citizens’ vehicles. A number of students remained gathered in the city square, insisting on reaching their centers to sit for their exams.
Al-Bakour stressed that the governorate mobilized all available resources to safeguard the examination process in coordination with relevant ministries and authorities. He underscored the need to keep students away from disputes and polarization, asserting that their future must not be used as leverage. He described students’ futures as a “red line” and a collective responsibility.
Meanwhile, the Suweida–Damascus highway saw heightened security and relief deployments from the early morning hours. Personnel from Internal Security, Highway Patrol, Civil Defense and the Syrian Arab Red Crescent worked to secure the movement of students and citizens and remove obstacles preventing access to exam centers.
The Ministry of Education confirmed that the exceptional session is proceeding as scheduled. It said all arrangements had been completed, including the delivery of exam materials, the arrival of invigilators and staff, and the provision of a safe and fair testing environment. The ministry expressed regret that some students were unable to reach their designated centers.
In a related statement, the United Nations in Syria welcomed Presidential Decree No. 163, which granted Suweida students an exceptional exam session. It voiced concern over reports of students being prevented from reaching their centers and other restrictions on freedom of movement.
The UN reaffirmed that every child has the right to education, learning and sitting for exams within a safe, stable and supportive environment. It called on all parties to ensure that students, supported by their caregivers, are able to exercise their right to education without pressure or obstacles that restrict their movement.
Suweida had prepared 27 exam centers for the exceptional session in its northern countryside, and the Syrian Arab Red Crescent announced its readiness to support the process and provide necessary requirements.
The makeup session is being held under Decree No. 163 of 2026, issued by President Ahmed al-Sharaa on August 19. The decree granted Suweida students who did not sit for the 2026 exams, or were unable to complete all subjects, an exceptional opportunity to take the basic and general secondary education certificate exams across all branches.
Official and UN statements converged on the urgent need to shield students from tensions and disputes, ensure their access to exam centers and enable them to sit for their exams — safeguarding their right to education and preventing field developments from jeopardizing their academic future.

items.title: Homs Mega-Project Draws Buyers as Questions Persist Over Developer and Execution
items.summary: Boulevard al-Nasr promises thousands of residential and commercial units, vast green spaces and a new landmark for Homs. Yet key details about the developer, main contractor, escrow arrangements and infrastructure financing remain unclear. The post Homs Mega-Project Draws Buyers as Questions Persist Over Developer and Execution first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Boulevard al-Nasr promises thousands of residential and commercial units, vast green spaces and a new landmark for Homs. Yet key details about the developer, main contractor, escrow arrangements and infrastructure financing remain unclear.
A major mixed-use development launched in Homs this month is attracting strong buyer interest and official support, while leaving important questions unanswered about the corporate structure, financing and execution capacity behind one of Syria’s most ambitious post-war construction ventures.
Boulevard al-Nasr, formally unveiled on 21 August 2026, is planned to include around 2,500 residential, commercial, administrative and hotel units, with approximately 500,000 square metres of above-ground construction.
Plans also envision roughly 250,000 square metres of underground parking for about 5,000 vehicles, alongside a public park approaching 350,000 square metres. Construction is scheduled to proceed in three phases, with completion targets at three, five and seven years.
The scale places the project among the most prominent reconstruction initiatives announced in Homs since the fall of the former Syrian government. Yet publicly available information reviewed for this investigation leaves several central issues unresolved.
One concerns the precise legal identity of the developer.
Material issued by Homs governorate in August 2025 referred to “Al-Omran for Real Estate Development and Investment”. The company’s website has used the same name, while another announcement on the site referred to “Al-Omran Holding”. At this month’s launch, Syria’s state news agency SANA identified Rifai Hammada as chairman of “Al-Omran Holding”, which it described as the company implementing the project.
The differing names do not necessarily indicate irregularity. Al-Omran Holding may be a parent company with a separate development subsidiary. However, publicly reviewed material does not clearly set out the legal relationship between the entities.
Nor does it provide the implementing company’s commercial registration number, jurisdiction of registration, declared capital, shareholder structure or a published copy of the final development agreement.
Some media reports have described Al-Omran as a Kuwaiti company established in 2006 and owned by Hammada. Yet several companies across the Arab world operate under the name Al-Omran or similar variants, making it difficult to attribute earlier corporate records to the Syrian project without documentation establishing the connection.
Hammada’s own business record is more readily documented.
Spanish corporate records show that HESCO European Group SL was established in 2021 with capital of €40,000, listing Rifai Hammada Abbara as its sole owner and sole administrator. Other Spanish records show engineering and property companies connected to him, while HESCO has a documented record of engineering and consultancy activity internationally.
This provides evidence of an identifiable engineering and commercial presence behind the Homs venture. It does not, however, automatically establish experience as the master developer of a project requiring large-scale financing, off-plan sales, contractor management, infrastructure delivery and the administration of thousands of buyers over several years.
Another unresolved question concerns the main construction contractor.
Publicly available announcements reviewed for the project identify Al-Omran as developer or implementing company and HESCO as involved in planning and urban design. They do not clearly identify a main contractor responsible for constructing the towers and infrastructure.
Such an appointment may still be under negotiation or may simply not have been announced. Yet for buyers committing money before completion, the identity and track record of the main contractor are important indicators of whether the project can move from design and sales to large-scale construction.
Financing arrangements are also drawing attention.

Russian drone kills utility worker and injures two children in Kherson
A 43-year-old employee of a municipal utility company was killed as a result of a Russian drone attack on Kherson's Korabelnyi district. Another utility worker and two children have sustained injuries.
Source: Oleksandr Prokudin, Head of Kherson Oblast Military Administration; Yaroslav Shanko, Head of Kherson City Military Administration; Kherson Oblast Military Administration; Kherson City Military Administration
Details: According to local authorities, Russian forces attacked the 43-year-old employee of a municipal utility company with a drone at approximately 12:00.
The man was taken to hospital in an extremely serious condition, but he could not be saved. His injuries proved fatal.
"My condolences to the family and loved ones of the deceased," Prokudin said.
Update: Kherson City Military Administration later reported that another municipal utility worker had been injured in the same drone attack.
A 31-year-old man was taken to hospital with blast injuries. Medical staff are carrying out further examinations on him.
Subsequently, the Oblast Military Administration reported another attack on the Kherson's Korabelnyi district.
At around 13:40, Russian forces attacked the area with a drone. Two children, aged 2 and 12, were caught in the attack.
Early reports indicate that both sustained blast injuries, while the older child also suffered a leg injury.
Doctors assess both children as being in a moderate condition. They are receiving the necessary medical care.
Background: One person was killed as a result of a Russian FPV drone attack on a vehicle in Kherson.

items.title: EU points out that €90bn loan will cover only two-thirds of Ukraine's needs
items.summary: The European Commission says its €90 billion loan to Ukraine covers two-thirds of the country's budgetary and defence needs for 2026-2027.
items.body_text:
EU points out that €90bn loan will cover only two-thirds of Ukraine's needs
The European Union's €90 billion loan to Ukraine for 2026-2027 has been designed to cover two-thirds of the country's budgetary and defence needs, and the EU is currently focused on disbursing the funds under the loan.
Source: European Commission chief spokesperson Paula Pinho, responding to a question about the prospects of covering Ukraine's defence budget shortfall, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The EU is continuing disbursements under the two-year €90 billion loan, which is intended to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's budgetary and defence needs.
Quote: "When we put forward the €90 billion loan for Ukraine, the idea was indeed that it covers budgetary and defence needs for 2026-2027, two-thirds of it. That's the calculation that it would be covering two-thirds of the needs of Ukraine in these domains for the two years."
Details: Pinho noted that "there is one third which cannot be covered by the EU and where we have been urging our partners to come in and step in".
The EU's chief spokesperson also pointed out that "these disbursements are also linked to the reforms that are being introduced in Ukraine", calling this "a critical aspect".
Quote: "We are making very good progress in that disbursement based on the requests that are being assessed from Ukraine, but again linked to the reforms that are gradually being introduced. So it is already extremely ambitious."
"[We are] well acknowledging the extreme needs of Ukraine and well acknowledging the situation on the ground, and we know very well that there are very, very strong needs by Ukraine in order to be in a position to deter further aggression, but we are focused now on what is already a very ambitious disbursement plan, and for the moment that's where our focus lies."
Background:
- The EU previously said that Ukraine had not submitted a formal request to the European Commission for an early disbursement in 2026 of the portion of the €90 billion loan earmarked for 2027, which would be used to cover Ukraine's €27 billion defence budget shortfall this year.
- On 24 August, the European Commission approved €6.1 billion in defence procurement for Ukraine under the EU's €90 billion loan.
- The EU is expected to disburse around €20 billion to Ukraine by the end of 2026, with new tranches potentially arriving in the coming weeks.
- On 30 July, the Council of the EU approved an updated reform plan under the Ukraine Facility mechanism, allowing Ukraine to receive €8.3 billion in 2026 to cover budgetary needs.

items.title: EU ambassador says she now sleeps in bathroom due to Russian attacks on Kyiv
items.summary: EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarína Mathernová has said intensifying Russian attacks on Kyiv have forced her to start sleeping in the bathroom.
items.body_text:
EU ambassador says she now sleeps in bathroom due to Russian attacks on Kyiv
EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarína Mathernová has said that she no longer sleeps in her bed due to Russia's ongoing attacks on Kyiv and has been forced to take shelter in the bathroom. She also described the consequences of last night's attack on the capital.
Source: Mathernová on Facebook, as reported by European Pravda
Quote: "I don't sleep in my bed anymore. I fall asleep on a mattress in the bathroom. It is the safest place in my hotel room.
I am tired. Sometimes scared. But I am not complaining. Kyiv is my mission. And knowing everything I know today, I would still choose no other diplomatic posting.
But the intensity of these attacks is becoming very difficult. People are exhausted. Cities are exhausted. The whole country is living under permanent stress."
Details: In her post, Mathernová also enumerated the consequences of last night's missile strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.
The ambassador added: "Ukraine does not need to be told to be resilient. Ukrainians have proven that every single day. They need to be able to sleep."
Background:
- Eight people were killed and five injured in Russia's attack on Kyiv on the night of 31 August-1 September.
- Earlier, Mathernová shared her impressions of an attack on Kyiv on the night of 1-2 July, when Russia also struck an area where many diplomats live.

items.title: Zelensky visits school in Kyiv region, urges partners to respond more actively to Russian attacks
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on international partners to respond more actively to Russian attacks and stressed that diplomacy must remain active even while officials from partner countries are on vacation.
items.body_text:
Zelensky visits school in Kyiv region, urges partners to respond more actively to Russian attacks
The head of state made the remarks after visiting a school in the Kyiv region to mark the start of the new school year, Ukrinform reports, citing the Office of the President of Ukraine.
Zelensky said that over the past two weeks, Russian forces had been striking infrastructure, including with the aim of disrupting the start of the school year. At the same time, he noted that most partners were on vacation and were effectively not responding to the ongoing Russian strikes.
"I believe that if there were international signals, then even on September 1... The Russians, apart from our Armed Forces, are also somewhat afraid when diplomacy speaks loudly. It is very unfortunate that some people are on vacation while others are fighting for their lives," he said.
Zelensky also said that Russia continued to attack Ukraine despite the start of the school year and was making children participants in the war.
"Even among any enemies, there is an understanding that children are children. But the Russians are making children participants in the war. They have done this, unfortunately, and will continue to do so until they are put in their place," he said.
Because of a Russian air attack, teachers had to conduct the first lessons in a shelter, including the nationwide lesson "The Language of Dignity: Seeing the Person Behind the Words" for first- through fourth-grade students. Zelensky joined the children in completing a quest and wished them a successful school year.
"I congratulate our first-graders on September 1 – they are absolutely brave – as well as their parents, all schoolchildren and our unbreakable state. It is very important that children went to school, and it is very important that so much has been prepared," Zelensky said.
He also thanked parents who, despite air raid alerts and Russian attacks, remain in Ukraine and work with teachers to ensure that children can continue their education at home, in Ukraine.
"I don't really like using the word 'socialization,' because when speaking to children, I want to say that they are making friends, that they are among their own, among equally cheerful and energetic children. It is good to see them talking to one another and having everything they need. Of course, we very much want these schools not to be built simply for the sake of construction. We want children to be able to use this infrastructure," Zelensky added.
According to the Office of the President of Ukraine, Zelensky was also shown an exhibition featuring photographs of the school that Russian forces destroyed in March 2022. It was not restored until the fall of last year. In addition to a shelter, the school has been equipped with an independent power supply in case of outages, modern educational spaces and sports facilities, while its cafeteria has also been renovated. Meals are provided as part of a reform implemented under the patronage of First Lady Olena Zelenska, which provides free hot meals for all students. The president thanked the cafeteria staff and the school community for their work.
"Children should have everything. I am very glad that there is a modern kitchen and that the children have everything they need. What they don't have is the most important thing – peace. That's true. We will certainly do everything to make that happen," Zelensky said.
September 1 is celebrated in Ukraine as Knowledge Day.

items.body_text:
General Staff: Russian army lost over 124,000 troops this summer, 25% more than in spring
Ukrinform
    Russian occupation forces lost 124,170 personnel at the front over the three summer months, including more than 42,000 in August.
    According to Ukrinform, the press service of the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces reported this on Telegram.
"In total, the enemy lost 124,170 personnel over the three summer months. The losses amounted to 39,290 in June, 42,860 in July and 42,020 in August. Thus, during the three summer months of 2026, the Ukrainian Defense Forces inflicted 25.8% more personnel losses on the enemy than during the corresponding period in spring," the General Staff said.
Russia's total combat losses since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, stood at approximately 1,489,640 personnel as of September 1, 2026, including 1,440 troops killed or wounded on August 31.

items.title: Graham’s ‘Sanctions Bill From Hell’ Against Russia Hits House Roadblock
items.summary: Graham’s “sanctions bill from hell” passed the Senate 86-11 but is now facing a major roadblock in the House. The bill would let Trump impose tariffs of up to 500% on countries buying Russian energy, but both Democrats and some Republicans are pushing back.
items.body_text:
A Russia sanctions bill that passed the US Senate by an overwhelming 86-11 vote is now in trouble in the House, where it faces opposition from Democrats and a lack of enthusiasm among Republicans.
The bill, championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, was supposed to give President Donald Trump more leverage to pressure Moscow to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
What Graham’s bill would do?
At its core, the legislation would allow the US president to impose tariffs of up to 500% on goods imported from countries that buy Russian oil, gas, uranium, and other key commodities.
That is the bill’s biggest weapon: rather than only punishing Russia directly, it threatens countries that keep trading with Moscow.
The measure would also expand the US sanctions regime against Russian entities and people supporting the war and give the president broader tools to target Russia’s economic partners.
Supporters say the threat of massive tariffs could force countries such as China and India to reduce their purchases of Russian energy – cutting one of Moscow’s most important sources of revenue.
The bill is named after Graham, who spent years pushing for tougher sanctions on Russia. He called the legislation a way to give the US president a powerful economic weapon against Moscow and its supporters.
The Senate said yes. The House isn’t rushing.
The bill passed the Senate on Aug. 7 with a rare bipartisan majority of 86-11.
But the momentum has largely disappeared in the House. House Republican leaders did not even put it on this week’s voting schedule.
Ukraine’s War Chest Shrinks as Europe Mulls Gamble with Russia Billions
Lawmakers returned to Capitol Hill on Monday after a five-week summer break, but the Russia sanctions bill was barely mentioned.
“We just came from a chairmen’s meeting, and nobody brought it up,” House Rules Chair Virginia Foxx, R-N.C., told Politico.
Asked whether the bill could move through her committee, Foxx said: “I have no idea. Nobody’s talking about it.”
Speaker Mike Johnson was no more committed.
“We’ll see,” he said when asked whether the House would vote on the bill.
That leaves Graham’s signature Russia sanctions push hanging in the balance just weeks after it won broad bipartisan support in the Senate.
Democrats fear giving Trump more power
The bill would give Trump new tools to punish Russia and countries that continue doing major business with Moscow, including new tariff powers.
Its supporters say those powers could help Trump put pressure on Russian President Vladimir Putin and force Moscow toward an end to the war.
But Democrats say Trump already has enough authority to sanction Russia and its economic partners.
House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Greg Meeks and Ways and Means Committee ranking member Richard Neal were among senior Democrats opposing the bill.
They warned that the legislation would give Trump additional tariff powers they believe his administration could abuse.
“Congress does not need to greenlight new tariff authority for the President,” they said.
Republicans are split
The bill also faces resistance from Republicans.
Some conservative lawmakers who have opposed US support for Ukraine said they have not even looked at the legislation.
Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., said he had not seen or heard about it.
“All I can say is in 14 years I’ve never voted to sanction a sovereign country,” Massie said.
Other Republicans are pushing House leaders to act.
Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a defense hawk who is retiring from Congress, said passing the bill is important.
“I think it’s very important to pass the sanctions bill,” Bacon said. “It’s a failure to not do so.”
The bill could also face procedural hurdles. House leaders could try to fast-track it, but that would require a two-thirds majority – meaning Democrats would need to provide significant support.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday

items.title: Sporting Diplomacy in Odesa: Ukrainian Servicemen Take on Italian Pacifists
items.summary: What happens when a group of Italian pacifists comes to a battered Ukrainian city to play soccer against Ukrainian soldiers in a tournament of the “beautiful game”? An encounter worthy of many toasts – with both Ukrainian and Italian wine.
items.body_text:
Odesa was the setting for a friendly sporting encounter between Italians and Ukrainians: a football match pitting Ukrainian servicemen against Italian activists from a civic movement committed to non-violent action. It was an unusual example of informal Italian diplomacy – and, at the same time, of civic courage.
From August 25 to 28, Odesa was cheerfully invaded by more than 130 activists from MEAN, the European Nonviolent Action Movement. The initiative probably caused a few headaches at the Italian Embassy in Kyiv, which goes to considerable lengths to discourage Italians from travelling to Ukraine on safety grounds. Yet it is worth emphasizing just how much it means to Ukrainians to meet foreigners willing to come and support their country at their own risk.
And the risk was very real. On two of the three nights of their stay, Russian forces launched kamikaze drones at central Odesa, striking precisely the areas where some members of the Italian group were staying. For people unused to air-raid warnings, those two frightening nights certainly lent the mission an added touch of realism.
The purpose of the MEAN mission – the Italian acronym carries a rather unfortunate meaning in English – was to demonstrate civil resistance to war and peaceful support for Ukraine. The activists visited cities battered by Russian attacks and took part in a series of activities and meetings with residents and local institutions. MEAN had previously travelled to Kyiv and Kharkiv as well.
‘Russia Always Calculates Its Strikes to Destroy Lives’: Zelensky Says After Deadly Overnight Attack
Among the many events organized in Odesa was a five-a-side football tournament held on Aug. 27, the final day of the visit. It was arranged in partnership with the International Association of Defenders of Ukraine and took place at Odesa’s Academy Sports stadium.
The Italians were hardly going to pass up an opportunity to play football. Someone observed, with a certain irony, that Italians have not had many chances to compete abroad lately – a reference to the national team’s absence from the World Cup. During their stay in Odesa, the activists therefore hastily assembled two Italian sides with suitably evocative names: “Civilian Corps” and “Nonviolent Action.” Waiting for them on the pitch were teams representing the Ukrainian Navy and Air Defense Forces.
The Ukrainian organizers staged the occasion with considerable ceremony. The Ukrainian Navy band welcomed the Italian visitors and played both national anthems.
In the square facing the assembled teams, the customary minute’s silence was observed for the fallen. Senior military representatives of the host association then addressed those present, followed by six military chaplains representing different faiths, each of whom offered a prayer before play began.
The teams played four matches, including the semi-finals and final. In the end, the superior fitness of the young servicemen – who play regularly – prevailed over that of the Italian teams, which had been assembled for the occasion. The Italians nevertheless compensated for their lack of training with their country’s natural calling for football, scoring several goals that gave their opponents something to think about.
At the awards ceremony, the Italian visitors were overwhelmed with gifts, while the Ukrainian winners received artistically crafted trophies made in Italy. Flags were exchanged as mementoes of the occasion: Italian flags for those of Ukraine and the Ukrainian Navy.
In a moment of unintended irony, the captains of the Italian pacifist teams were presented with two large bronze cylinders decorated with the Ukrainian trident and commemorative inscriptions. The objects were, in fact, two empty artillery shell casings – a reminder that even an instrument of war can be transformed into a work of art and a symbol of friendship.
Col. Andriy Maydachenko, the highest-ranking Ukrainian officer present, gave an oversized bottle of Ukrainian craft wine

items.title: Budanov Predicts Russian Drone Attacks Will Last Until State Duma Elections
items.summary: Kyrylo Budanov said Russia is likely to continue mass drone attacks on Ukraine at least until its State Duma elections in September, as Moscow seeks to show voters a "picture of victory" despite lacking battlefield gains.
