items.title: Vietnamese lecturer turns her Chinese mastery into fully funded PhD scholarship
items.summary: A Vietnamese lecturer has secured a fully funded PhD scholarship in China after mastering advanced Chinese and developing a research proposal on how learners acquire thousands of Chinese words.
items.body_text:
Duong Thi Hong Nhung, 25, won the prestigious Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) with an HSK 8 certificate, just seven points short of the highest level's 390.
The lecturer at the Department of Chinese Language at Phenikaa University in Hanoi learned about the scholarship in May. She will study at Beijing Normal University (BNU), which describes itself as a "key university" directly under China’s Ministry of Education and being "among the country's leading institutions for teacher education."
Under the CSC scholarship, Nhung’s tuition, accommodation and health insurance will be fully covered, and she will receive a monthly living allowance of 3,500 yuan (US$487).
Nhung said she was not surprised by the result, as she had anticipated it following her interview with the admissions panel.
"They kept asking in depth about my research topic, which I considered a positive sign," she said.
Nhung earned a master’s degree in International Chinese Language Education at BNU on a CSC scholarship two years ago. To pursue a PhD, she applied to become a lecturer at Phenikaa University’s Department of Chinese Language, where she could gain teaching experience, supervise students’ research, write academic papers and spend time building her application profile.
Pham Thuy Hong, deputy head of the Department of Chinese Language at Phenikaa, said Nhung is a highly regarded young lecturer with expertise, research capabilities and a strong sense of responsibility.
"She uses modern teaching methods, inspires students and is very enthusiastic about all the department’s work," Hong said.
All of Nhung’s choices at the time were aimed at pursuing higher education. Preparing her application was also the busiest period of her life as a lecturer. At times, she slept only three to four hours a day.
"The pressure was so intense that sometimes I busted into tears while working," Nhung said.
She said research ability is what admissions panels care about most when evaluating PhD applications. She therefore invested heavily in her research proposal.
Nhung initially planned to study the Chinese phonetics of Vietnamese speakers. After months of reading materials and discussing the topic with lecturers, she shifted her focus to the cognitive processes involved in vocabulary acquisition among Chinese language learners. She believes the topic offers long-term research potential and still contains many gaps.
"The research direction I choose for my PhD will affect my entire academic career, so I want to make the choice carefully," Nhung said.
She subsequently prepared a detailed research plan outlining the procedures and specific methodologies, along with a reference list of 40 to 60 sources.
Nhung also traveled to China to take the HSK, an international Chinese-language proficiency test with nine levels. Despite studying for only about 10 days, she scored 383 on HSK 8, just seven points short of the highest level.
She believes differences in Chinese proficiency among learners mainly stem from vocabulary. To reach HSK levels 7, 8 or 9, learners need to acquire around 12,000 words while also practicing with test papers to become familiar with the exam structure and time allocation.
For the essay section, she practiced writing from a native speaker’s perspective and used AI tools to evaluate and revise her writing.
For students hoping to win scholarships, she recommends preparing early rather than waiting until their final year of university. In addition to GPA and language certificates, applicants should invest in a research proposal if they plan to pursue a master’s or doctoral degree.
Thai Linh, also a Chinese language lecturer at Phenikaa, said she was not surprised that her colleague had won the PhD scholarship.
"What I admire most about Nhung is her discipline and commitment to self-study. Outside teaching hours, she almost exclusively reads materials, writes and conducts research," Linh said.
In early September, Nhung will move to Beijing to begin her studies. Sh

items.title: Vietnam sets world record after 1.77 million people join nationwide walk
items.summary: The second nationwide “Marching Forward with Vietnam” event on Aug. 30 brought together 1,774,268 people across all 34 provinces and cities, setting a Guinness World Record for the largest number of localities simultaneously organizing walking activities to raise environmental awareness.
items.body_text:
The event was organized by Nhan Dan Newspaper and the Ministry of Public Security, with the participation of the Ministry of National Defense and the Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union Central Committee. In Hanoi, it took place at Dong Kinh Nghia Thuc Square and Ba Dinh Square.
Participants recorded nearly 10.07 billion steps at walking events held in nearly 3,000 communes, wards and special zones nationwide.
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Gen. Phan Van Giang praised the programme’s creative approach and asked organizers to develop it into an annual activity linked with patriotic emulation movements and major national campaigns.
He said the participation of millions of people will help build momentum for a stronger, more prosperous, civilized and happy Vietnam.
Le Quoc Minh, member of the Party Central Committee, Editor-in-Chief of Nhan Dan Newspaper, Vice Chairman of the Party Central Committee's Commission for Publicity and Chairman of the Vietnam Journalists Association, said the programme’s second edition marked an important step toward turning the event into a lasting social habit.
Deputy Minister of Public Security Sen. Lieut. Gen. Le Van Tuyen described the programme as a practical initiative to promote healthy lifestyles, improve public health and strengthen awareness of environmental protection and community responsibility.
The 2026 programme, launched on Aug. 12, forms part of the "10 billion green steps – For a sustainable Vietnam" campaign, encouraging people to exercise while adopting greener habits such as saving energy, sorting waste, planting trees and reducing carbon emissions.
In central Nghe An Province, tens of thousands of officials, members of the armed forces and residents joined the event at Ho Chi Minh Square in Truong Vinh Ward on Aug. 30. Following a flag-raising ceremony and the national anthem, participants walked from the square along Truong Thi Street and back.
All communes and wards in Nghe An organized activities in response, with universities and colleges also mobilizing large numbers of staff, Youth Union members and students.
The programme also featured communications and experiential activities on net zero, climate change, green development and the circular economy, aiming to promote public awareness of environmental protection and sustainable development.

items.title: India’s top court drops criminal cases against protesters
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 1 — India’s Supreme Court called off criminal investigations today against most of the prote...
items.body_text:
NEW DELHI, Sept 1 — India’s Supreme Court called off criminal investigations today against most of the protesters who took part in demonstrations over the leak of a medical exam paper that forced the resignation of the education minister.
The court invoked its special constitutional powers to provide relief to protesters who joined demonstrations led by the online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement in July.
The demonstrations turned violent when police clashed with tens of thousands of protesters in New Delhi on July 20 as they tried to march towards the parliament.
Clashes also broke out in other states, including Bihar and West Bengal.
Police filed cases against hundreds of students, accusing them of rioting, violence and damaging public property.
“If both sides show good faith, then all issues can be resolved one by one,” Chief Justice Surya Kant said as he passed the order.
The court also directed the government to provide compensation within three months to the families of students who reportedly died by suicide following the exam paper leak.
Following the court’s directions today, the CJP said it was withdrawing its plans for a protest in Delhi on Saturday, Ashutosh Ranka, a CJP spokesman, said in a statement.
However, investigations would continue against 2,873 protesters who have prior criminal records, the Press Trust of India reported.
The demonstrations were sparked by anger over the paper leak, but grew into a wider movement over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what critics describe as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s increasingly authoritarian rule.
The protests proved to be the biggest challenge that Modi has faced after winning a third term in 2024. — AFP

items.title: Qatar urges US, Iran to resume talks after flare-up
items.summary: DOHA, Sept 1 — Mediator Qatar today urged the United States and Iran to return to negotiations after they renewed...
items.body_text:
DOHA, Sept 1 — Mediator Qatar today urged the United States and Iran to return to negotiations after they renewed tit-for-tat attacks.
On Sunday, the US carried out strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran quickly retaliating by attacking US military targets in the Middle East.
After six months of war, the foes remain at an impasse, with Iran disrupting traffic in the strategic Strait of Hormuz with its blockade and the US persisting with a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
“We have said from day one that leaving the issue unresolved and trying to normalise the closure of the Strait would lead to escalation,” Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told a regular press briefing.
“This is precisely what we have witnessed over the past two days,” he said.
“We urge the parties to exercise wisdom and return to the negotiating path, and we continue to intensify our efforts with our mediation partners to ensure a return to that path.”
Earlier today, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would “immediately” reciprocate if the United States returned to a June deal aimed at ending their war.
“In Qatar, in the region, in the world today, we cannot afford to accept the status quo,” Al Ansari said.
“Discussions with our mediation partners — whether in Pakistan or Oman — are ongoing,” he added.
Last week, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani travelled to Tehran as part of the mediation efforts, after Iran and Oman, which border the key strait, said they were discussing a temporary shipping corridor and the clearance of mines. — AFP

items.title: Too much crime: Thailand shortens visa-free stays for dozens of nations from Sept 15
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 1 — Thailand will halve the length of visa-free stays for tourists from more than 60 countries and t...
items.body_text:
BANGKOK, Sept 1 — Thailand will halve the length of visa-free stays for tourists from more than 60 countries and territories to 30 days, effective September 15, the foreign ministry said today.
Tourism is vital to the Southeast Asian nation’s economy, but officials say the move is part of an effort to curb crime involving foreign nationals.
A string of recent arrests has included foreigners accused of drug offences, sex trafficking and operating businesses such as hotels and schools without proper permits.
Under Thailand’s current tourism scheme, travellers from more than 90 countries — including Europe’s 29-nation Schengen area, China, India, the United States and several South American countries — are eligible to visit for up to 60 days without a visa.
The reduction to 30 days visa-free applies to over 60 countries and territories, including China, the United States and 27 EU countries, the Thai foreign ministry’s consular affairs department said on Tuesday.
The visa-free status for around 20 other countries was unclear, with a foreign ministry official declining to comment on Tuesday.
Visitors from Peru, Brazil and South Korea will be granted 90-day visa-free stays, up from 60 previously.
Tourists will be able to extend their stays once, at the discretion of an immigration officer, a government spokeswoman told AFP in May when the cabinet approved the measure.
Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said that month that the plan to trim visa-free visits was part of a crackdown on individuals abusing the visa system by committing crimes in the country.
Thailand has attracted 20.9 million foreign tourists since the beginning of the year, down three per cent on the same period in 2025, according to the latest official figures. — AFP

items.title: Oncology firm Novocure says cyberattack exposed US patient records
items.body_text:
Oncology firm Novocure says cyberattack exposed US patient records
Sept 1 : Oncology company Novocure said on Tuesday a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to certain information systems in mid-August exposed internal records of more than 1,400 U.S. patients.
The breach adds to a growing number of cyberattacks on the healthcare sector, including medical device makers Abbott, Stryker Medtronic and Boston Scientific, drugmaker Novo Nordisk and drug-delivery equipment supplier West Pharmaceutical Services.
Here are some more details:
• Novocure said it activated its cybersecurity response plan, implemented containment measures and initiated an internal investigation of the event.
• The exposed data included internal company patient ID numbers and general contact information for healthcare providers the company works with and for Novocure employees such as their job titles and phone numbers.
• Data for fewer than 50 other patients in the western U.S. that included additional identifying information was also exposed.
• The company said access to its medical treatment devices was not obtained, and that all its systems are fully functional.
• Novocure does not expect this cybersecurity incident to have a material impact on its financials.

items.title: Philippine couple married in hip-deep floodwaters
items.summary: One photo showed a boy holding the wedding rings walking down the aisle — with floodwater up to his waist.
items.body_text:
Philippine couple married in hip-deep floodwaters
One photo showed a boy holding the wedding rings walking down the aisle — with floodwater up to his waist.
HAGONOY: A Philippine couple tied the knot on Tuesday (Sep 1) at a Catholic church swamped in hip-deep waters, as heavy rains have pummelled large parts of the country for a month.
Clutching a bouquet of white blooms and clad in an off-shoulder white gown, Leian Lieza Galang gingerly waded into the murky brown floodwaters inside the Saint John the Baptist church in Hagonoy town, north of Manila, to wed Gilbert Chico.
The parish priest declared the couple, both in their 30s, husband and wife at an abbreviated late-morning ceremony, said wedding photographer Mikko Rey Alfonso, who witnessed his first flooded wedding experience at the parish.
"The parish had advised them to postpone the wedding due to the rising floodwaters from upstream. It was their decision to proceed," Alfonso told AFP, adding the church had been partially underwater for nearly a month.
"Since they wanted to see it through, we the servants of the parish did the best we could to make this a special day for them."
Heavier-than-usual seasonal monsoon rains pounded the northern third of the mainly Catholic archipelago in August, with resulting landslides and flash floods killing 34 people, according to the latest official tally.
"They love each other. Nothing could stop their union," Alfonso said.
The couple did not respond to questions from AFP.
A video clip of the wedding posted on the parish's Facebook page showed the bride being hugged by her parents in front of empty pews adorned with plastic flower bouquets.
One photo showed a boy holding the wedding rings walking down the aisle — with floodwater up to his waist.
The bride arrived in the church aboard a rickshaw with an elevated chassis, keeping her wedding gown pristine before she got off at the church courtyard, Alfonso said.
To allow her to safely navigate the floodwaters, "the bride ... had to have her wedding gown altered to shorten the train", he added.
He said fewer than 15 people were in attendance.

items.title: Ukraine parliament fails to pass parcel tax law tied to IMF, EU funding
items.summary: KYIV, Sept 1 - Ukraine's parliament failed on Tuesday to pass a law to introduce taxes for foreign parcels that is required to unlock IMF and EU funds, dismissing government warnings about growing financial risks and a shortfall in funding for defence needs.
items.body_text:
Ukraine parliament fails to pass parcel tax law tied to IMF, EU funding
KYIV, Sept 1 - Ukraine's parliament failed on Tuesday to pass a law to introduce taxes for foreign parcels that is required to unlock IMF and EU funds, dismissing government warnings about growing financial risks and a shortfall in funding for defence needs.
Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said Ukraine faced a $27 billion deficit for its defence needs and financial risks were mounting. He called on lawmakers to speed up voting on key reform legislation.
An IMF monitoring mission is in Ukraine this week to review its lending programme.
"We have $30 billion – this is the amount we can, and should receive from our partners this year, provided we fulfil the commitments we have made. The relevant decisions are in our hands ..." Koretskyi said at the start of a parliamentary session.
"Not all decisions that we agreed with our partners have been made, and our obligations to them have not been fully met. Unless these issues are resolved, the country may face significant financial risks."
The government needed 226 votes for it to pass but got only 194. It was not immediately clear how many lawmakers voted against the bill, or were absent from the session.
SOME LAWMAKERS POINT TO COST OF LIVING
The issue of taxing foreign parcels has become very sensitive in Ukraine's talks with its lenders.
Currently, parcels containing goods worth less than €150($175) are not subject to taxes in Ukraine. Introducing the tax would generate around 10 billion hryvnias ($227.53 million) annually, the finance ministry has previously said.
Some parliamentarians fear that new taxes would further raise the cost of living for people already battered by the war. Others argue that it will help domestic producers by helping reduce consumer imports.
Danylo Hetmantsev, head of the parliamentary committee for finances, taxes and customs, said that the price of the failure to pass the legislation was about €4 billion from the EU and the IMF.
It was not immediately clear what he based that figure on. The next tranches of funds are due to be determined in the review.
"A financial disaster is not just around the corner. It is already in the room," he said on the Telegram app after the vote.
As the war with Russia drags on and gets more expensive, financial challenges mount for Ukraine.
Russia intensified its strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, and wartime damage to businesses and the economy is growing. The capital Kyiv was under the sixth consecutive day of Russian strikes on Tuesday. REUTERS

items.title: Zambia's chaotic election casts shadow over Hichilema swearing-in
items.summary: LUSAKA, Sept 1 - Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema was sworn in for a second term on Tuesday, while his main rival was in prison on treason charges, the conclusion of a chaotic vote observers said was marred by serious irregularities.
items.body_text:
Zambia's chaotic election casts shadow over Hichilema swearing-in
LUSAKA, Sept 1 - Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema was sworn in for a second term on Tuesday, while his main rival was in prison on treason charges, the conclusion of a chaotic vote observers said was marred by serious irregularities.
Hichilema came to power in 2021 pledging a democratic break from a government he accused of rigging elections and jailing opponents.
But observers have cited a number of irregularities during and after the August 13 election, including fiddling with the vote tally, the arrest of opposition lawmakers, the posting of soldiers at polling stations and the shutting down of courts, while runner-up Brian Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, were both charged with treason over the weekend.
Zambia, a major copper producer, is a focus of competition between China and the United States on account of its mineral wealth. Both Beijing and Washington congratulated Hichilema on his win and sent representatives to his inauguration.
Zambia has held regular, if flawed, elections since the 1990s. Analysts said the latest could set a precedent that makes it easier for future leaders to entrench their power, rather than deliver the democratic renewal Hichilema had promised.
"Zambia's democratic credentials are in peril. We have never experienced this kind of confusion," said historian Euston Chiputa, referring to the suspension of vote counting, the positioning of the military at counting centers and the subsequent arrests of opposition members.
UNANSWERED QUESTIONS SURROUND OPPOSITION ARRESTS
Reports by international and local election observers found indications that votes were added to Hichilema's tally, although they all found that he would have won regardless.
Asked about such criticism, the Electoral Commission of Zambia told Reuters that the courts should examine any allegations of discrepancies.
But as the deadline approached for such a case to be filed last week, Zambian authorities barred access to the courts and later said that no complaint had been received.
Authorities have provided few details about their claims against Mundubile and around a dozen other opposition members who were jailed, saying only that they were linked to suspected national security threats and that some had been in possession of weapons. They provided no evidence for the assertion.
A lawyer for the accused said they would defend themselves in court.
INVESTORS LOOK PAST TURMOIL
The reports of election irregularities and the detention of opposition figures have done little to dent investor appetite.
Since the election, Zambia's eurobonds have returned 0.8% in dollar terms, outpacing the Africa average of 0.3%, according to JPMorgan bond index data.
Citi upgraded Zambia's international bonds to overweight days after the vote and said it plans to buy local government debt, while foreign investors who had pulled back before the election have since returned.
Hichilema steered Zambia through a debt restructuring and economic recovery in his first term, making him the preferred choice for investors seeking policy continuity.
"There might be a bit of short-sightedness here," said Christopher Vandome, a senior research fellow at Chatham House.
"Longer term, this isn't really a good example of the institutional strengthening ... that can lead to long-lasting investment environments." REUTERS

items.title: Tehran presses US to honour deal as Trump threatens to hit Iran ‘hard’
items.summary: Tehran says it will uphold the truce if Washington does, as new attacks revive fears of a wider war.
items.body_text:
Tehran presses US to honour deal as Trump threatens to hit Iran ‘hard’
- Iran will reciprocate if the US honours its commitments under the June interim deal, but tensions remain high after recent missile exchanges.
- Both sides are avoiding a full-scale war but warn of harsh responses to further attacks, risking escalation from economic conflict to military action.
- Iran faces economic challenges with a plunging currency and high inflation, but claims sufficient foreign reserves and readiness to stabilise markets.
AI generated
DUBAI – Iran has said it will reciprocate if the United States honours its commitments under a June interim deal on halting their conflict, but tensions remain high after US President Donald Trump threatened Tehran with further strikes.
The six-month-old conflict has shifted into an economic stand-off before a US attack on Iran’s Larak island on Aug 30, which Iran responded to by launching missiles overnight at two US air bases in Jordan.
“We’re going to hit them hard. There will be a response,” a Fox News reporter quoted Trump as saying on Aug 31, although Trump separately told reporters that the renewed strikes did not signal a return to full-scale war.
A senior Iranian source said the exchanges of fire were a “limited and contained confrontation”, but he added that Tehran would deliver a harsh response if attacked again.
While neither side appears to want a return to all-out war, their pledges to respond to further attacks highlight how quickly a conflict that has increasingly been fought through sanctions, blockades and economic pressure can spill back into military action.
Tehran has repeatedly said it will allow free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz only if Washington implements the terms of the memorandum of understanding (MOU) that both sides signed in June but quickly unravelled.
The MOU declared an end to fighting but deferred many of the most difficult issues and paved the way for a broader 60-day negotiation period, which passed without further agreement.
“I am stating clearly that if the US returns to its commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate,” Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said.
He was speaking in Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, during a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, whose members also include Russia, China, India and Pakistan.
He also said on Aug 31 that war was in no one’s interest, and that Tehran was still open to a negotiated solution.
But there has been no sign of a breakthrough, and the heightened tensions this week have renewed fears of oil supply disruptions from the world’s key crude-producing region, with Brent futures rising another 1.3 per cent on Sept 1.
“The tit-for-tat missile exchanges between the US and Iran bring validation to those who believe that even if not a ‘forever war’, this conflict will run and run,” said PVM analyst John Evans.
Highlighting such concerns, two supertankers carrying Saudi oil were struck by unknown projectiles within minutes of each other while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz late on Aug 31, according to data from shipping intelligence and tracking firms Marisks and Kpler.
Thousands have been killed in the conflict, mainly in Iran and Lebanon, since it began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28.
Washington has increasingly relied on economic pressure to try to force Tehran to stop blockading Hormuz and end the conflict.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned that countries doing business with Iran could face US sanctions, adding that secondary sanctions are likely to be unveiled weekly in the effort to pressure Iran, with an initial focus on banks.
Iran’s central bank governor, Abdolnaser Hemmati, said on Sept 1 that Tehran has sufficient foreign currency reserves.
The central bank is ready to inject up to US$2 billion (S$2.5 billion) into the foreign exchange market to calm recent volatility, Hemmati was quote

items.title: Ministry maximizing defense spending
items.body_text:
- 
            Ministry maximizing defense spendingMILITARY BUILDUP: Aside from this year’s budget, the defense ministry detailed its mid-term plan to upgrade, develop and procure defense materiel amid Chinese threats
  - By William Hetherington / Staff writer, with CNA
 The military is reviewing budget execution trends and postponing non-urgent projects to maximize defense spending, the Ministry of National Defense said yesterday as it submitted its budget for next year and other defense documents to the legislature. The ministry said China’s “gray zone” harassment of Taiwan has intensified while its military capabilities continue to expand rapidly. The assessment was included in its “Five-Year Force Buildup and Administration Plan Report” (五年兵力整建及施政計畫報告), submitted alongside the defense budget for this year and the “2026 China Military Power Report” (中共軍力報告書). China continues joint combat-readiness patrols, military exercises and China Coast Guard operations, while using maritime militia forces, legal and psychological warfare, and economic coercion. These activities seek to treat the Taiwan Strait as internal waters and strengthen military deterrence against Taiwan, while improving Beijing’s ability to transition from training to combat, the ministry said. An undated photograph shows a Strong Bow anti-ballistic missile (Sky Bow IV) being launched.Photo: Screen grab from the Web site of National Chungshan Institute of Science and Technology The ministry’s domestic priorities include new rifles, night-vision optics, portable counter-drone systems, wheeled combat vehicles and armored fighting vehicles (AFVs). The military is upgrading submarines and testing the domestically built Hai Kun (海鯤), while developing rescue and replenishment vessels, drones and uncrewed boats. It is to procure the Strong Bow (強弓) medium-range anti-tactical ballistic missile system and build a multilayered air-defense network under the “Taiwan Shield” (T-Dome) framework. Other priorities include the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK), upgraded air-combat training systems, digitized command and communications networks, and an islandwide fiber-optic backup network. US procurement priorities include M109A7 self-propelled howitzers and HIMARS multiple-launch rocket systems. The military will continue acquiring Altius 600M and Switchblade 300 systems, and add Altius 600ISR and 700M attack drones. The army has budgeted NT$57.07 billion (US$1.8 billion) from next year to 2033 for 178 domestically developed Cheetah (獵豹) AFVs, armed with 105mm cannons. The D3 prototype has passed evaluation, with procurement to begin next year. The vehicles will have a maximum speed of 100kph, a range of 500km and the ability to fire while moving. The army is also to spend NT$10.7 billion from next year to 2032 on 4,647 light tactical off-road vehicles. Another NT$79.54 billion from next year to 2034 is budgeted to replace aging CM21 armored personnel carriers with 410 wheeled combat and command vehicles. The navy has budgeted NT$18.28 billion from next year to 2032 for a follow-on oil and ammunition replenishment ship. It operates the Panshih (磐石) and Wuyi (武夷), which entered service in 2015 and 1990 respectively, with the Wuyi nearing the end of its service life. It will also spend NT$21.16 billion from next year to 2034 on two follow-on rescue vessels, as existing ships are more than 80 years old. Another NT$13.85 billion is budgeted for a submarine rescue vessel as the Hai Kun and subsequent domestically built submarines enter service. The air force has budgeted NT$36.04 billion this year to 2032 for the Strong Bow medium-range anti-tactical ballistic missile system, previously funded through classified allocations. The system is designed to intercept tactical ballistic missiles at ranges of up to 1,000km and will be integrated with lower-tier systems to form a multilayered defense network. Delivery is scheduled to begin in 2028, although the number of systems remains classified.

items.title: Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040
items.body_text:
- 
            Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040
  - By Esme Yeh / Staff writer, with CNA
 President William Lai’s (賴清德) administration plans to allocate more than NT$40 billion (US$1.26 billion) next year to develop 10 major artificial intelligence (AI) projects, with a goal of training at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. Lai yesterday met with the VIS Mars robotics team, which represented Taiwan at the FIRST Tech Challenge robotics tournament in Turkey in June. He praised the students for overcoming a major setback when customs detained their competition equipment after they arrived in Turkey. Unable to access their robot, the team collected discarded components and borrowed tools from other teams to assemble a replacement robot before the competition. They won four qualification matches and earned the tournament’s highest match points. President William Lai, center, and members of the VIS Mars Robotics Research Club pose for a photograph at the Presidential Office in Taipei yesterday.Photo courtesy of the Presidential Office Lai said the students’ ability to adapt under pressure reminded him of the fictional character MacGyver. Team captain Ray Shang (商泱瑞) said their greatest strength was not their equipment, but their ability to rethink, adapt and solve problems regardless of the circumstances. Lai said technology education and talent development remain key government priorities. The government launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development and data-driven approaches. The initiative, together with the 10 major AI projects, aims to build a large AI talent pool, promote smart applications across industries and strengthen Taiwan’s competitiveness. Shang said the team’s experience showed that perseverance and teamwork were more important than having perfect equipment. The team had advanced through competitions in Hong Kong and the Netherlands before facing its biggest test in Turkey. Meanwhile, Minister of Digital Affairs Lin Yi-ching (林宜敬) said Taiwan could accumulate computing capacity of at least 10,000 graphics processing units (GPUs) within a year through private investment in AI computing centers under a build-own-operate (BOO) project launched by the ministry. Technological sovereignty does not mean developing every technology domestically, he said. Instead, Taiwan should focus on critical technologies, particularly sovereign AI and low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite communications, he said. Sovereign AI means AI systems used in Taiwan should understand Taiwanese perspectives, society and languages. The ministry is therefore developing a Taiwan sovereign AI training corpus by making government-owned datasets available to local and international researchers. AI computing centers should be located in Taiwan so that AI models can operate under Taiwanese laws and regulations, Lin said, adding that the ministry has designated such centers as major public infrastructure eligible for private investment. LEO satellite communications are another priority, he said. Taiwan needs independent communication capabilities, as submarine cables could be disrupted during conflict or “gray zone” harassment. Although Starlink has shown limited interest in Taiwan’s commercial market because of its strong 4G and 5G coverage, Lin said LEO technology remains essential to Taiwan’s technological sovereignty and national resilience.

items.title: Nvidia to invest US$3.5 billion in MediaTek
items.body_text:
- 
            Nvidia to invest US$3.5 billion in MediaTek
  - Bloomberg
 Nvidia Corp is investing US$3.5 billion into MediaTek Inc (聯發科), deepening collaboration with the Taiwanese chip designer at a time when it’s working to persuade more companies to build chips that plug into its dominant data center ecosystem. Nvidia will buy bonds convertible into MediaTek shares, the companies said in a joint statement yesterday. The investment broadens a partnership between the two chip designers that will see MediaTek using NVLink Fusion and the newly announced NVHBM technology as part of an Nvidia tech suite to help components communicate more seamlessly in data centers. The Taiwanese company is trying to challenge Broadcom Inc and Marvell Technology Inc by helping owners of data centers create their own components. Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang, left, joins MediaTek Inc CEO Rick Tsai at a news conference in Taipei on June 2.Photo: CNA For Nvidia, the new agreement is the latest effort to ensure the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is built around its hardware platform and standards. The US chip giant has been building data center interconnect systems like NVLink Fusion and partnering with the likes of MediaTek to ensure it maintains a central role in the entire hardware chain, not just with its class-leading AI accelerators. The MediaTek agreement follows a similar announcement by Amazon.com Inc, which agreed to deploy an additional 2 million Nvidia components. Critically, Amazon also pledged to use Nvidia’s connection technology with its in-house chips. Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang (黃仁勳), who was born in Taiwan, is tightening ties with a company working to reduce its reliance on the smartphone market. MediaTek earlier this year secured a partnership with Alphabet Inc’s Google, and is gaining credibility as a design partner to major tech firms that are seeking to build their own AI chips. That momentum has led the chipmaker’s market value to roughly triple in recent months. The agreements with MediaTek and Amazon give Nvidia the opportunity to retain its central role in the build-out of AI data centers even when companies are deploying chips designed to replace its main offerings. The deal is yet another example of Nvidia’s leadership investing in customers, rivals and other companies involved in the AI industry. Concern about the seemingly circular nature of those investments has percolated in investor circles, though Nvidia has strongly disputed the idea it’s creating false demand. MediaTek already works with Nvidia on the US chipmaker’s nascent effort to get into the laptop industry. The Taiwanese company is helping with Nvidia’s RTX Spark product for that market. MediaTek has also signaled that it plans to hire aggressively to better capture business opportunities from the AI boom. Forecasting AI chip revenue of about US$2 billion this year, the company has set the goal of securing as much as 15 percent of an US$80 billion segment of the data center market next year.

items.body_text:
China says solar power capacity surpasses coal for first time
China, the world’s largest emitter of greenhouse gases that drive climate change, has pledged to peak carbon emissions by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.
China’s installed solar energy capacity has surpassed that of coal-fired power for the first time, the national energy body said Tuesday, hailing the milestone.
China, the world’s largest emitter of greenhouse gases that drive climate change, has pledged to peak carbon emissions by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.
“As of the end of July this year, China’s installed solar power capacity reached 1.286 billion kilowatts,” the National Energy Administration (NEA) said.
“For the first time, photovoltaic installed capacity surpassed coal-fired power, becoming the largest power source category in China,” it added.
The country’s coal-fired power installed capacity, the energy body said, stood at 1.285 billion kilowatts.
Solar generation rose 15.5 percent on-year in the first seven months of 2026 to 802.4 billion kilowatt-hours, about one-eighth of the country’s total, the NEA said in another statement.
It did not detail in these statements what the total generation of coal-powered energy was for the first seven months of this year.
The NEA said China’s installed solar power capacity and power generation “have maintained a steady trend of rapid growth”, with it playing an “increasingly prominent role” in guaranteeing electricity supply and driving the energy transition.
Coal has been China’s key power generation source for decades and a key driver of its planet-warming emissions.
But the country’s coal-fired power generation fell by nearly two percent in 2025, despite rising energy demand in the world’s largest emitter, data reviewed by AFP showed in February.
It marked the first decline in six years, with some analysts saying it was the first time on record that coal generation dropped at the same time as power demand rose.
China has seen an explosive growth in its renewable installation, with coal’s share in its energy mix edging down in recent years.
The country installed a record 315 gigawatts of solar power and 119 gigawatts of wind power capacity last year — over 80 percent of total newly installed power generation capacity, according to the China Electricity Council.

items.title: Hong Kong Int’l School and US church founder reach settlement over financial mismanagement lawsuit
items.summary: Hong Kong International School (HKIS) and its US-based founder have reached an out-of-court settlement, after the latter sued the school last year for alleged financial mismanagement and over accusations it served only an “elite” section of the city’s population. The school will no longer be governed by its founder, The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod (LCMS), but […]
items.body_text:
Hong Kong International School (HKIS) and its US-based founder have reached an out-of-court settlement, after the latter sued the school last year for alleged financial mismanagement and over accusations it served only an “elite” section of the city’s population.
The school will no longer be governed by its founder, The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod (LCMS), but will continue to provide an “American-style education grounded in the Christian faith,” a letter sent to parents on Tuesday read.
HKIS board of managers chairperson Harold Kim, who wrote the letter, said the school remained in a strong financial position and the settlement would not affect tuition fees.
The latest development brings to a close a lawsuit filed by the LCMS at the High Court in September last year. While the major US church body originally entered Hong Kong in 1949 to provide services for the local community, in particular mainland Chinese refugees, it later expanded its role and founded HKIS in 1966 to target expatriate families.
Today, HKIS has two campuses, one in Repulse Bay and another in Tai Tam, and is known for providing an American-style curriculum.
LCMS sued Hong Kong International School Association Limited (HKISAL) – the school’s operator – over “serious concerns” regarding its finances and what the church deemed to be transparency and leadership issues.
HKIS holds more than HK$2.8 billion in financial reserves and serves “only a small, elite section of Hong Kong,” going against the school’s original mission of being open to “all children,” the LCMS said then.
‘Uncertainty and anxiety’
In the email to parents on Tuesday, Harold Kim said the school acknowledged the LCMS’s role in the founding of HKIS, as well as its contribution to establishing the Christian identity that continues to shape HKIS.
“The past 11 months have brought uncertainty and anxiety to our community, and we are grateful for the support of and trust in HKIS that you have shown throughout this period,” Kim wrote.
In an FAQ for parents, the school stated that the lease for the Repulse Bay campus was still in the LCMS’s name, but that procedures were underway for the lease to be transferred to HKISAL.
When the LCMS filed the lawsuit, there was concern that the school could potentially be evicted from its Repulse Bay campus. The Tai Tam campus lease is held by HKISAL.
The LCMS will also no longer pursue the establishment of Hong Kong Pacific School. The body had said earlier that it would set up a new school by that name if HKISAL failed to address its concerns. A website that was previously set up for Hong Kong Pacific School is no longer accessible.
In a statement published on Monday, the LCMS confirmed that the dispute with HKISAL had been resolved with the church group “recouping a monetary reflection of its historical inputs to the school in order to advance the mission of the church by other means.”
“The outcome provides a fair resolution to the concerns the LCMS has raised for many years. It also enables the LCMS to pursue its mission unencumbered by the dispute with HKISAL, so that we can best utilize our resources going forward,” said LCMS Board of Directors Chair Christian Preus.

items.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
items.summary: The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels. Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris from a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping […]
items.body_text:
The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.
Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris from a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and gouging a path of destruction through Nepal.
Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a race against time in treacherous conditions to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.
So far, only corpses have been pulled out of tunnels blocked with sludge.
“We are focused on search and rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing,” Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman, told AFP on Tuesday.
“Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease.”
With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, the authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling. At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers far downstream in India.
Embed from Getty Images
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.
‘Find their bodies’
In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives, posting photographs on a long wall outside a hospital, in the fading hope of finding them alive.
Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, came to post photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and granddaughter who went missing in the town of Trishuli Bazaar, after being swept away by last week’s surge.
A warning alert sounded, but the elderly woman was “too old to run”, he recounts.
“Her granddaughter was helping her escape but both were swept away.”
Sapkota says he no longer has “any hope that they survived”, after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.
“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said, holding up photos of the two missing women dressed in traditional clothes.
Embed from Getty Images
In Chitwan district, mourning relatives cremated some of the dead.
Soldiers were seen unloading bodies of victims from helicopters in Nepal’s Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.
Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.
“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.
Embed from Getty Images
‘Climate change’
In Nuwakot, AFP photographers on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud into the rubble of their homes for usable items, some clearing away dirt and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in the ruins.
Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming more than 30 nations.
They include tourists who had come for trekking in the apparently serene Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people — that has contributed little to the emissions driving global warming churned out by wealthy and industrialised nations, but is suffering its consequences.
“It is now time for us to strongly raise with the international community the issue of the disasters we are experiencing as a result of climate change,” Shah, Nepal’s prime minister, said in a statement late Monday.
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.
Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale, with Kathmandu warning reconstruction costs could run into the “billions of dollars”.
‘Mourn the victims’
Nepal said 987 bodies had been recovered, and listed 3,916 as missing.

items.body_text:
UK ex-PM Starmer to quit parliament, focus on ‘international affairs’
Keir Starmer was deeply unpopular during his two years in power, and eventually had to step down after multiple missteps
Britain’s former prime minister Keir Starmer, who stepped down as leader this summer after a tumultuous two years in power, announced on Tuesday he would quit parliament to focus on “international affairs”.
In a statement on social media, Starmer said it was the “right time” to resign as the MP for the Holborn and St Pancras seat in London after 11 years, triggering a by-election.
“It is now time to step aside and focus on other issues: international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast-changing world,” Starmer said in his statement.
His constituency’s local newspaper, the Camden New Journal, reported Starmer had informed the Labour Party of his decision to leave parliament after 11 years, six of those as leader of the party.
Andy Burnham was parachuted into the prime minister role in July to take over from Starmer, who announced his resignation amid piling pressure from fellow Labour MPs.
Starmer, a former human rights lawyer, is credited with reviving the centre-left Labour Party, helping it win a landslide victory in general elections in 2024.
But the strait-laced politician was deeply unpopular during his two years in power, and eventually had to step down after multiple missteps, making way for the next leader in Britain’s churn of prime ministers.

items.body_text:
Norway’s King Haakon VIII swears allegiance to constitution
Haakon’s wife Queen Mette-Marit, 53, was not beside her husband as she is still recovering from her June 17 transplant
Norway’s King Haakon VIII took an oath before parliament on Tuesday, the first major institutional step of his reign, though his wife, still convalescing after a lung transplant, was unable to attend.
Dressed in a ceremonial uniform, the 53-year-old Haakon, who became king when his father King Harald V died on Friday morning aged 89, swore to abide by the Scandinavian country’s constitution, under which the royals have a primarily symbolic function.
“I promise and swear that I will govern the Kingdom of Norway in accordance with its Constitution and Laws, so help me God, the almighty and omniscient,” he recited in the parliament’s main chamber.
Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, 53, was not beside her husband as she is still recovering from her June 17 transplant.
Dr. Are Holm, head of the Pulmonary Department at Oslo University Hospital, said in a statement from the palace that complications after a transplant are not “uncommon”.
“The queen has had complications on several occasions since the operation, including today,” Holm said.

items.body_text:
Call for Trump-Xi AI safety talks comes as state media slams US AI governance
Dean Ball, a former White House adviser, says the window for cooperation will ‘widen’ in next few months but will not stay open forever
“I have always believed US/China AI safety collaboration would be desirable but thought it was unlikely to happen,” Dean Ball, OpenAI’s head of strategic futures, wrote on X on Tuesday. “In the past few months, though, the ground has shifted. There is a window of opportunity.”
Ball, a former adviser to the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said the window for cooperation would “widen over at least the next few months” because of escalating AI risks and the upcoming bilateral meeting, but warned it “will not remain open forever”.
Ahead of Xi’s planned state visit to the US on September 24, officials from both sides “will press forward with dialogues” on topics including AI guardrails, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on Sunday.
However, Chinese state media delivered a harsh critique of US AI governance ahead of the talks.
In an article published on Sunday, Yuyuan Tantian, a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster CCTV, accused US AI firm Anthropic of trying to dictate industry rules through aggressive lobbying and CEO Dario Amodei’s calls to arm democracies with AI.

items.body_text:
日本核廢料選址第5案 經濟產業省選中茨城縣大宮市
日本核廢料存放選址第五案，將在茨城縣常陸大宮市進行調查。示意圖。（資料照）
日本核廢料最終處置場選址卡關20多年，經濟產業省8月31日再出手，向茨城縣常陸大宮市提出第一階段「文獻調查」申請。這是繼東京都小笠原村南鳥島後，國家主導的第2例、全國第5例。市長鈴木定幸回應個人相當正面看待，但會先徵詢議會與居民意見。
文獻調查是選址3階段中的第一步，需費時約2年，透過地質圖資與文獻確認當地是否有火山、活斷層等紀錄，之後才會進入約4年的概要調查與約14年的精密調查。日本因採行核燃料循環政策，會將用過核燃料回收鈾、鈽後，將剩餘高輻射廢液以玻璃固化暫存，最終目標是埋入地下300公尺深處地層隔離數萬年。該制度自2002年開放地方自願申請後進展緩慢，直到2017年公布科學特性地圖後，才從2020年起陸續有自治體加入。
經濟產業省選中常陸大宮市的理由，是該市被評為「具有較高可能性確認到合適特性的地區」，其中南東部在運輸面也被認為有利。該市位於茨城縣西北部、人口約3萬5千人，且部分區域位於東海第二核電廠30公里圈內，已有完整的疏散計畫。即便如此，地方仍有分歧，有居民認為應先確認安全性再與全體市民商議，也有居民坦言若其他地區都反對，核廢料最終將無處可去。
目前已有4處完成或正在進行文獻調查，分別是北海道壽都町、神惠內村、佐賀縣玄海町與東京都小笠原村南鳥島，常陸大宮市若接受將成為第5處，政府目標未來擴大至10處左右。接受調查的自治體最高可獲20億日圓交付金。此事也引發青森縣關注，宮下知事肯定國家展現主導姿態，但強調暫存的核廢料有保管期限壓力，期盼中央能加速決定最終處置地，讓核燃料循環政策能持續推進。

柯文哲陪艋舺服飾商圈掃街 洪文和挺吳怡萱推商圈數位轉型
前民眾黨主席柯文哲（左）向艋舺服飾商圈店家拜票懇請支持。（記者孫唯容攝）
九合一選舉今（1）日倒數88天，民眾黨「台北隊」議員黃瀞瑩、林珍羽、陳宥丞、張志豪，以及參選人吳怡萱、許甫，由前黨主席柯文哲、黨主席黃國昌等人帶領上午赴選委會領表，下午柯文哲陪同吳怡萱前往艋舺服飾商圈拜票，向在地店家懇託，不少店家熱烈歡迎，與柯文哲握手，台北市商圈產業聯合會榮譽理事長洪文和也到場相挺，洪文和認為吳怡萱對在地商圈整合有想法，希望也給予新人吳怡萱機會。

洪文和表示，在艋舺地區最主要依然是「服飾跟小吃」的串聯，比如說，可以讓民眾來買衣服的話，送一張50元折價券在地特約店家消費美食，因為萬華都是以銅板經濟為主，以庶民小吃來行銷，剛好可以搭得上，很有機會成功。

items.body_text:
台中年編6億養護樹木2年卻少2.2萬棵 議員質疑降溫「增綠」淪口號
中市年編6億進行樹木養護，張芬郁（中）等質疑2年來樹木卻大減2.2萬棵。（記者蘇孟娟攝）
台中市民近來感受經常看到砍樹、樹木被剃頭景象，夏日無遮蔭引關注，市議員張芬郁質疑，建設局年編6億養護樹木，但全市登錄的樹木資料2年來少了2.2萬棵，城市降溫的三帖特效藥「引風、增綠、留藍」淪於政策口號；建設局指出，因持續校正更新枯死、病蟲害、風倒及具公共安全疑慮等樹木移除資料致，並非大規模砍樹。
包括市議員張芬郁、陳雅惠、謝家宜等關切建設局對於公園樹木、行道樹的養護管理，張芬郁指出，建設局每年編列至少6億養護全市23萬棵樹，也設置「友善樹木空間管理資訊系統」讓每棵樹有戶籍，但資訊紊亂不真實。
張芬郁表示，2024年資料庫登錄的樹木資料有24萬6768棵，目前只剩22萬4052棵，2年來少了2.2萬棵，今年5月素有「台中香榭大道」之稱的大隆路移除了29棵小葉欖仁，但這些已移除的樹木目前還在資料庫中，大里草湖路有一排木棉樹，卻不在資料庫中，充斥幽靈樹籍假戶口。
張芬郁指出，樹木持續減少，台中市長盧秀燕把「引風、增綠、留藍」稱為城市降溫的「三帖特效藥」淪於政策口號，市民並未感受氣溫降低，只看見在砍樹和樹木被剃頭。
建設局長陳大田表示，修剪樹木有作業指南，除了防颱高空修剪，一定要保留樹冠和生長樹勢，建設局116年編列6億3千萬，不只用於種樹也用於公園綠地養護；建設局指出，近兩年系統樹籍數量減少約2.2萬株，主要因持續辦理樹木普查及樹籍資料校正，並同步更新枯死、病蟲害（如褐根病）、風倒及具公共安全疑慮等樹木移除資料，相關數量變化為樹籍資料校正及樹木動態管理所致，並非大規模砍伐樹木。

items.title: Russia adds $6 million in canopies to North Korea border project as costs soar
items.summary: Russia’s new border crossing is facing additional costs with the addition of nearly $6 million worth of canopies, taking its ballooning budget to at least $183 million, nearly twice the original sum the Russian government allocated for the project. Records published on Monday by Rosgranstroy, the Russian state agency overseeing the project, via a state […]
items.body_text:
New procurement records add millions more to budget that has nearly doubled, as Moscow targets early September opening
		
		
Russia’s new border crossing is facing additional costs with the addition of nearly $6 million worth of canopies, taking its ballooning budget to at least $183 million, nearly twice the original sum the Russian government allocated for the project.
Records published on Monday by Rosgranstroy, the Russian state agency overseeing the project, via a state procurement portal reveal that seven canopies will be added at a cost of $5.8 million.
Red circles represent the sites for prospective canopies relative to the border facility captured in satellite imagery and as seen through its blueprint | Images: Planet Labs, edited by NK News, Rosgranstroy
The new canopies are expected to sit on either side of the main building, at the vehicle inspection site, at sites for detained vehicles and at both entrances to shield “vehicles and personnel from rain or snow” and “facilitate inspections.”
They will be added to the largely completed modular buildings at the site, previously seen in satellite imagery by late August. While work is ongoing on the Russian side, the DPRK completed its border facility early in the summer.
The Russian checkpoint was estimated to be 65% completed as of last month, ahead of the bridge’s expected opening in early September.
The new canopies are not the only additions set to increase the project’s total cost. Similar procurement records show that Rosgranstroy tasked Moscow-based proprietor Pavel Zakipnykh with conducting an “expert examination” of the crossing’s modular buildings for $600,000 last week.
The border construction authority also sought subcontractors to supply and install diesel generators and fuel storage for $1.3 million, conduct an expert analysis of the security system for $500,000, install information and navigation signs for $2.3 million and provide a modular electrical substation for another $500,000.
NK Pro previously reported that the checkpoint’s officially disclosed costs quickly ballooned far above the initial budget of some $100 million Moscow set aside in early 2025, reaching at least $173 million by Jan. 2026.
Russia and North Korea were expected to open the crossing by June 19, the second anniversary of the 2024 Vladimir Putin-Kim Jong Un summit, but the project faced delays. The two sides officially connected their respective sections of the bridge in April.
In late July, a Russian official from the bordering Khasan settlement said the opening would take place some time in early September, possibly to coincide with the Sept. 1-4 Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, with Putin expected to attend.
It is not clear whether Putin’s agenda will include the bridge’s opening ceremony or if the project has even been completed. 
Apart from the delays and ballooning costs, the project has recently faced other headwinds, including a $1.5 million lawsuit filed against its main contractor TonnelYuzhStroi by one of its material suppliers.
Edited by Alannah Hill

items.title: New customs route opens for cars in North Korea, but brokers stay cool
items.summary: North Korea has begun allowing new cars to be imported from China through official customs channels, but few brokers are eager to take advantage of the change, as new vehicles carry thin profit margins and slow returns compared with the used cars whose imports remain suspended. “Hyesan recently started allowing new car imports through customs,” […]
items.body_text:
North Korea has begun allowing new cars to be imported from China through official customs channels, but few brokers are eager to take advantage of the change, as new vehicles carry thin profit margins and slow returns compared with the used cars whose imports remain suspended.
“Hyesan recently started allowing new car imports through customs,” a source in Ryanggang province told Daily NK on Monday, referring to a border city that has long served as a hub for informal trade with China. “But compared to used cars, you have to put in a lot of money for not much return, so it’s not an exaggeration to say there are almost no brokers willing to invest fresh capital to get into this.”
Vehicles are among the items whose supply, sale and transfer to North Korea are restricted under United Nations Security Council sanctions imposed over the country’s nuclear and missile programs. In Ryanggang province, which borders China, vehicles have long been brought in through an unofficial channel known as state smuggling, informal trade that operates with the tacit tolerance of local officials. Since July 20, however, vehicles have been allowed to enter through customs, though only new cars can currently be imported officially, according to the source.
The problem, brokers say, is that new cars are simply less profitable than used ones.
Slim margins make new cars a hard sell
Because the purchase price of new cars in China is clearly known, brokers have little room to mark up prices when reselling them in North Korea. Profits can shrink further when multiple brokers import similar models at the same time and end up competing for buyers. As a result, brokers are focused on selling off the new car inventory they already have rather than investing fresh capital to bring in more.
Used cars, by contrast, vary widely in price even for the same make and model year, depending on mileage, the condition of the engine and transmission, whether major parts have been replaced, and features like heating and air conditioning. Because the resale price in North Korea can shift depending on how a car’s condition and strengths are presented, brokers have relatively more room to turn a profit than with new cars.
A man in his 50s with experience importing vehicles said, “Even when we brought in cars through state smuggling, we handled far more used cars than new ones, but now used cars can’t be imported through customs or through smuggling.” He added, “Bringing in a single new car costs more than 100,000 Chinese yuan (about $14,870), but it’s not easy to even make 5,000 yuan (about $745) in profit.”
He said the purchase price for used sedans in China ranges widely, from the 60,000 yuan (about $8,920) range to more than 100,000 yuan (about $14,870). “Selling one usually nets somewhere between 7,000 yuan (about $1,040) and 10,000 yuan (about $1,490) in profit, and with good luck, you can make even more.”
Brokers also favor used cars because their lower price tags make them sell faster than new ones. The shorter turnaround between importing and selling a vehicle gives brokers a clear advantage when it comes to cash flow.
As a result, even though new car imports through customs are now permitted, brokers are reportedly more focused on when they will be able to bring in the used cars they have already purchased but have not been able to collect. With used car imports suspended, the money brokers sank into vehicles already bought in China has been tied up for an extended period.
Brokers are said to be hoping a solution emerges soon, whether that means resuming used car imports through state smuggling or through official customs channels. Rumors circulated this month that new measures on the used car import issue were imminent, but with no sign of movement, brokers’ frustration is reportedly deepening.
“Brokers who already bought used cars in China are completely focused on when they’ll be able to bring them in, whether through customs or state smuggling,” the source said.

items.title: North Korean official kills coworker to hide embezzlement scheme
items.summary: A North Korean official under investigation for embezzling state property killed a subordinate earlier this month after panicking that the employee’s testimony would expose his wrongdoing to internal inspectors, Daily NK has learned. A source in South Pyongan province told Daily NK on Monday that the “shocking” killing took place in mid-August at the printing […]
items.body_text:
A North Korean official under investigation for embezzling state property killed a subordinate earlier this month after panicking that the employee’s testimony would expose his wrongdoing to internal inspectors, Daily NK has learned.
A source in South Pyongan province told Daily NK on Monday that the “shocking” killing took place in mid-August at the printing plant of the South Pyongan Ilbo, the newspaper published by the provincial branch of the ruling Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK). The official was under internal review for embezzling state property and reportedly feared his misconduct was about to be fully exposed.
The case surfaced after higher authorities detected signs that the official had been embezzling printing paper and other materials belonging to the state, prompting a formal investigation.
According to the source, the official got into an argument with a subordinate who had gathered decisive evidence and testimony proving his wrongdoing while the inspection was underway. The subordinate had reportedly watched the official’s misconduct unfold over time and grew increasingly anxious as the probe deepened, worried he could be implicated as an accomplice, and punished alongside his superior, simply for having worked under him, despite never taking part in any wrongdoing himself.
Argument turns deadly
During the argument, the subordinate methodically laid out the misdeeds he had witnessed. Gripped by extreme fear that full exposure to inspectors would bring severe punishment, the official impulsively killed him.
The official had reportedly been secretly siphoning off state-owned paper and materials from the factory for personal gain for some time. As the investigation closed in and the pressure mounted, he committed an even graver crime on impulse.
When the commotion broke out, factory staff and public safety officers, North Korea’s police force under the Ministry of Social Security, who were elsewhere on site rushed to the scene. The victim was rushed to a hospital but had already died.
Residents of the village near the factory who learned of the case sharply criticized the official, reportedly saying he “stole state property to satisfy his own greed, let his family put on airs, and in the end even took the life of an innocent person.”
The source said harsh, sweeping punishment is expected not only for the official but also for others linked to the embezzlement of state property. The case is also likely to trigger a hard-line special inspection by the party of the entire publishing and printing sector across South Pyongan province.
Reporting from inside North Korea
Daily NK operates networks of sources inside North Korea who document events in real-time and transmit information through secure channels. Unlike reporting based on state media, satellite imagery, or defector accounts from years past, our journalism comes directly from people currently living under the regime. We verify reports through multiple independent sources and cross-reference details before publication.
Our sources remain anonymous because contact with foreign media is treated as a capital offense in North Korea — discovery means imprisonment or execution. This network-based approach allows Daily NK to report on developments other outlets cannot access: market trends, policy implementation, public sentiment, and daily realities that never appear in official narratives.
Maintaining these secure communication channels and protecting source identities requires specialized protocols and constant vigilance. Daily NK serves as a bridge between North Koreans and the outside world, documenting what’s happening inside one of the world’s most closed societies.

items.title: Cheap North Korean coal keeps flowing into China despite U.N. ban
items.summary: North Korea’s mineral exports to China have recently increased, as Beijing appears to be enforcing sanctions on the North less strictly amid warming ties between the two countries. A source on North Korea told Daily NK on Friday that thousands of tons of North Korean coal were recently transferred to Chinese vessels through ship-to-ship transfers […]
items.body_text:
North Korea’s mineral exports to China have recently increased, as Beijing appears to be enforcing sanctions on the North less strictly amid warming ties between the two countries.
A source on North Korea told Daily NK on Friday that thousands of tons of North Korean coal were recently transferred to Chinese vessels through ship-to-ship transfers in waters near Nampo port. More than 3,000 tons of coal are smuggled out in a single night this way, the source said, and such shipments have gone out on consecutive days this month.
It is difficult to gauge exactly how much coal North Korea has exported, but Chinese traders involved in transporting the coal say the volume coming in from North Korea appears to have risen by 30% to 40% compared with last year.
The price of North Korean coal exported to China currently varies depending on calorific value, but generally runs around 500 Chinese yuan per ton.
According to Bloomberg, Australian coal was priced at $138 per ton and Chinese coal at $120 per ton as of Aug. 21. Converted to dollars, the 500 yuan per ton price of North Korean coal comes to about $74, roughly 46% cheaper than Australian coal and 38% cheaper than Chinese coal.
North Korean coal not only carries a price advantage but also benefits from lower shipping costs, given its proximity to China. If rising global coal prices continue to align with demand inside China, the incentive to seek out cheap North Korean coal is likely to persist.
A sanctions ban being routinely ignored
North Korea’s coal exports, however, are a clear violation of United Nations Security Council sanctions. The Security Council imposed a total ban on North Korean coal exports under Resolution 2371, adopted in August 2017.
Even so, the recent rise in North Korean coal entering China shows that Beijing’s willingness to enforce sanctions and crack down on smuggling has weakened considerably compared with the past. The fact that the coal is entering the country through indirect means, such as ship-to-ship transfers at sea rather than formal customs channels, is further evidence that China’s monitoring has grown lax.
Amid this, North Korea is also reported to be actively pursuing exports of rare minerals to China, not just coal. According to the source, large quantities of North Korean minerals such as molybdenum and magnesite are also flowing into China, with the trade taking place over land or by sea depending on the item and region.
In many cases, mineral trade conducted overland is reportedly led by state institutions, including North Korean consulates in China. According to the source, it is difficult for anyone other than state institutions or privileged agencies with official approval to take part in the mineral trade.
For North Korea, minerals are an export that can bring in foreign currency relatively quickly. Chinese companies, for their part, favor North Korean minerals for their low prices and the shipping advantages that come with proximity, meaning the interests of both sides align.
If Chinese authorities’ lax enforcement and monitoring continue, the flow of North Korean coal and minerals into China is likely to keep expanding. “Many North Korean trading companies involved in the mineral trade are operating in China,” the source said. “North Korea is eager to sell, and demand in China isn’t small either, so the trade will keep growing.”

items.title: Beach sprinting was just the start of Damien Cook's NRL story
items.summary: It's been a long time since Damien Cook was known merely as a beach sprint champion, but ahead of the champion hooker's final NRL game, all the old stories are being told one last time.
items.body_text:
analysis
Damien Cook's NRL legacy stretches from beach sprinting to the trail he leaves behind
With a bit of luck, they'll tell the old Damien Cook story one more time.
This weekend, the 35-year-old St George Illawarra skipper will play his final NRL match before heading to Super League side Castleford next year.
His farewell will be at Wollongong Showground, the closest ground in the league to the ocean. When the swell's big, you can almost hear the waves crashing on City Beach from the hill.
Maybe it will be when Cook runs out for the 263rd and last time, or perhaps he'll dart out from dummy half to take on the Parramatta defence with a glimpse of the old quickness.
Maybe it'll be the commentators who say it, maybe it'll just be fans in the stands, but someone, somewhere will almost certainly tell somebody else "you know, he used to be a champion beach sprinter."
It's a story nobody seems to tire of telling — Cook himself still hears about it all the time.
"It's the great Dane Gagai's fault. He mentioned it one day when I was doing media — a few people knew about it, but he said it real loud, the journo I was speaking to did a story on it and it got out from there," Cook said.
"It's never stopped; I still get it every day. Commentators say it, I get it in comments, DMs, Instagram stories; if people see a post about a beach sprinter they tag me in it. You have to laugh."
The yarn got its greatest play during Cook's ascent to becoming one of the best hookers in rugby league, which came almost 10 years ago now, and it's worth breaking it out one more time to celebrate the end of an NRL career with an extraordinarily long tail.
It took a while to get going. Cook spent plenty of time as a second-stringer on second-rate teams.
He did not make the run on side for an NRL match until he was almost 23 and wasn't a full-time starter at hooker until the year he turned 27.
But after taking the long way, he made up for lost time immediately, and once the beach sprinting tale got used up, we started to tell others.
Cook can't pick his favourite himself. He is overwhelmed by the memories he's made because there are so many.
This late starter has now played the seventh-most matches of any dummy half in the history of the game, so when you ask him about his favourite match there's so much to choose from.
There's the first grade debut back in 2013, of course, which came for St George Illawarra against Wests Tigers at the Sydney Cricket Ground in Heritage Round. The retro jerseys and brown football made it feel like history even while it was happening.
There was the first game at Wollongong a week later. Cook is proud to finish his NRL journey there, given it's where he grew up watching football and where he played his junior grand finals for Helensburgh.
In a nice full-circle moment, his first match there in the top grade came against the Eels, just like his last will.
"The big one that day was when I got under Fuifui Moi Moi — it wasn't me being brave, he was coming straight at me," Cook said.
"I didn't have much of a choice."
There's the late-season cameo for Canterbury in 2015, which first made Cook's name and proved he could ride the lightning, and his debut at South Sydney, where he played more than 200 games and spent his most glorious times.
There's his first State of Origin match in front of 90,000 at the MCG in 2018, when he was one of 11 New South Wales debutants alongside players like Nathan Cleary, Tom Trbojevic, Latrell Mitchell and Cameron Murray.
Cook was the best of them that night in a magnificent beginning, and he always seemed to find something extra for the Blues — among dummy halves, only Ben Elias and Danny Buderus have worn the jersey more.
The 2019 decider, when he scored a scorching try right through the heart of the Queensland defence, was perhaps his single greatest highlight in rep football, but playing for Australia against Tonga in Auckland later that season was another special night.
As the Tongan anthem rang out

items.title: Is Marnus Labuschagne finally out of luck?
items.summary: After spending years as one of the luckiest Test cricketers in the game, Marnus Labuschagne's fortunes appear to be turning and, unfortunately for him, so has his form.
items.body_text:
Will Marnus Labuschagne's recent fortunes see him out of the Test side?
For a period of 23 Tests, Marnus Labuschagne was statistically the luckiest batter in Test cricket.
He had more genuine chances dropped or missed than any other batter from his debut up until the end of the 2021/22 Ashes series. He was more often than not able to turn those reprieves into significant scores.
In more recent times, it's been slim pickings. In fact, it's been 23 Tests since his last century, dating back to the fourth Ashes Test at Old Trafford in 2023.
He's been left out of the ODI squad travelling to take on Zimbabwe and South Africa later this month. The right-hander has only missed five of Australia's last 56 ODIs, raising questions about his future in the Test side.
"We're still very much working through what that Test squad looks like, but I can say we separate out those formats," chair of selectors George Bailey told reporters when unveiling the ODI squad.
"He has played some really important one-day cricket for us; at his best that looks a certain way, but the way that squad and team is structuring up there just wasn't space for him."
If you break down Labuschagne's career into the period before his last Test ton and the period since, there is somewhat of a trend: his luck has seemingly run out.
Looking at only genuine chances missed by opposition teams — dropped catches, missed stumpings, opposition teams not reviewing a decision that would have seen him dismissed, or wickets on a no ball — he was given a reprieve 25 times from 75 innings where he faced at least one ball.
That's a chance every three innings from his Test debut in 2018 to his most recent hundred back in 2023.
Across his first 20 Tests he scored six centuries and 12 fifties, earning him a batting average of 62.15. If, in that time, he had been taken at the first opportunity, that average drops to 46.50.
In the 2019-2021 World Test Championship cycle, Labuschagne played 13 Tests and scored the most runs of any other batter in the world. He finished that period with 1,675 runs at an average of 72.82. Across the 23 innings he was required to bat in, he was afforded 12 chances, or one every 1.92 innings.
When you compare that with Steve Smith in the same period, he was given a reprieve four times, which equates to one every 5.5 innings. Smith was still able to score 1,341 runs in that WTC cycle, which highlights Labuschagne's ability to capitalise when given the opportunity.
In fact, his entire Test career has been based on it.
Labuschagne made his Test debut in 2018 due to the bans handed down to Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft after the sandpaper incident the last time Australia's Test team toured South Africa.
That put him in the frame for the 2019 Ashes squad and, after a red-hot Smith was hit in the neck by a Jofra Archer bouncer at Lord's, Labuschagne got his next chance as the first concussion substitute in the history of international cricket, courtesy of a rule introduced the month before the series started.
In the next Test in Leeds, Labuschagne was dropped on 14, 42 and 60, and England failed to review an edge that would have been given out when he was on 35. He went on to make 80.
That series, including that fortunate knock of 80 at Headingley, cemented his spot in the side, with Usman Khawaja the unfortunate one to make way when Smith returned, a decision that left Khawaja on the outer for three years.
His ability to turn a reprieve into a significant score was a hallmark of his early Test career. Labuschagne's maiden Test century came against Pakistan at the Gabba in 2019 when he scored an impressive 185 off 279 balls. Pakistan fans might still be ruing the fact he was dropped by Asad Shafiq on 33 that same innings.
In that WTC cycle alone, if he had been taken at the first opportunity, his batting average would drop to 55.68, which would have had him ranked 11th in the world.
